## Commercial performance

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Cold_Heart_\(Pnau_remix\)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Commercial performance")\]

In the United Kingdom, "Cold Heart (Pnau remix)" debuted at number 33 on the [UK singles chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_singles_chart "UK singles chart") in the issue dated 26 August 2021.[\[55\]](#cite_note-UK_Chart-55) The song reached number one, having spent three consecutive weeks at number two, with sales of 64,000, including 5.9 million streams and 5,000 copies on limited edition CD single, in its ninth week on the chart on 21 October.[\[55\]](#cite_note-UK_Chart-55)[\[56\]](#cite_note-United_Kingdom-56)[\[57\]](#cite_note-Ainsley-57) It represented Lipa's third chart-topping single in the UK, after "[New Rules](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Rules "New Rules")" (2017) and "[One Kiss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Kiss_\(song\) "One Kiss (song)")" (2018), and John's eighth and first in 16 years, since he was featured artist on American rapper [2Pac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tupac_Shakur "Tupac Shakur")'s posthumous single "[Ghetto Gospel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghetto_Gospel "Ghetto Gospel")" (2005).[\[57\]](#cite_note-Ainsley-57) John also became the first solo artist to achieve a top 10 single in six different decades, spanning from the [1970s](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1970s_in_music "1970s in music") to the [2020s](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020s_in_music "2020s in music").[\[58\]](#cite_note-58) In April 2023, the song received triple platinum certification from the [British Phonographic Industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Phonographic_Industry "British Phonographic Industry") (BPI) for shifting more than 1,800,000 units in the UK.[\[59\]](#cite_note-United_Kingdom_Cert-59) In Australia, "Cold Heart (Pnau remix)" reached number one on the [ARIA Singles Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ARIA_Charts "ARIA Charts") for 10 consecutive weeks as well as number one on the [New Zealand Singles Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Official_New_Zealand_Music_Chart "Official New Zealand Music Chart") in New Zealand.[\[60\]](#cite_note-Australia-60)[\[61\]](#cite_note-61)[\[62\]](#cite_note-New_Zealand-62) The song marked Lipa's first chart-topping single in Australia as well as John's first one since "[Something About the Way You Look Tonight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Something_About_the_Way_You_Look_Tonight "Something About the Way You Look Tonight")" / "[Candle in the Wind 1997](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Candle_in_the_Wind_1997 "Candle in the Wind 1997")" in 1997.[\[63\]](#cite_note-63) Also in 2022, it garnered a ten-times platinum certification from [Recorded Music New Zealand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recorded_Music_NZ "Recorded Music NZ") (RMNZ) in New Zealand for selling more than 300,000 units.[\[64\]](#cite_note-New_Zealand_Cert-64) In Australia, it was certified fifteen-times platinum by the [Australian Recording Industry Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Recording_Industry_Association "Australian Recording Industry Association") (ARIA) for selling 1,050,000 equivalent units.[\[65\]](#cite_note-Australia_Cert-65)

In Canada, "Cold Heart (Pnau remix)" reached number one on the [Canadian Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadian_Hot_100 "Canadian Hot 100") in the issue dated 8 January 2022, having spent a total of 12 consecutive weeks.[\[66\]](#cite_note-Canada-66)[\[67\]](#cite_note-67) The song also reached the top position on the [Canada AC, CHR/Top 40 and Hot AC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_charts#Canadian_charts "Billboard charts") rankings, respectively.[\[68\]](#cite_note-Canada_AC-68)[\[69\]](#cite_note-Canada_CHR-69)[\[70\]](#cite_note-Canada_HAC-70) In October 2022, it received a septuple platinum certification from [Music Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_Canada "Music Canada") (MC) for shifting more than 560,000 units in the Canada.[\[71\]](#cite_note-Canada_Cert-71) In the United States, "Cold Heart (Pnau January 2022, earning Lipa's fourth top 10 single on the chart and John's 28th entry.[\[72\]](#cite_note-United_States-72)[\[74\]](#cite_note-74) Topping the [Adult Contemporary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adult_Contemporary_\(chart\) "Adult Contemporary (chart)") and [Adult Top 40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adult_Top_40 "Adult Top 40") rankings,[\[75\]](#cite_note-BADC-75)[\[76\]](#cite_note-BADP-76) it further peaked at number one on the [Hot Dance/Electronic Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance/Electronic_Songs "Dance/Electronic Songs") chart, logging its 34th week at the top on 11 June.[\[77\]](#cite_note-BHDE-77)[\[78\]](#cite_note-78) In May 2022, the song garnered a double certification from the "**Cold Heart (Pnau remix)**" is a song by British singer and songwriter [Elton John](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John "Elton John"), recorded with [Dua Lipa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dua_Lipa "Dua Lipa") for the former's collaborative studio album _[The Lockdown Sessions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Lockdown_Sessions_\(Elton_John_album\) "The Lockdown Sessions (Elton John album)")_ (2021). It was released on 13 August 2021 as the [lead single](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lead_single "Lead single") from the album for [digital download](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_download "Music download") and [streaming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Streaming_media "Streaming media") in various countries by [EMI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EMI_Records "EMI Records") and [Mercury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercury_Records "Mercury Records"). Created during the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"), the collaboration between the artists was a testament to their friendship, which was established in November 2020. The song is a medley of four songs written by John and [Bernie Taupin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernie_Taupin "Bernie Taupin"), as well as Andrew Meecham, Dean Meredith, [Nicholas Littlemore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Littlemore "Nick Littlemore"), [Peter Mayes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Mayes "Peter Mayes") and [Sam Littlemore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Littlemore "Sam Littlemore"), with the production completed by the latter three as part of the dance music group [Pnau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pnau "Pnau"). A medley of John's songs "[Rocket Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocket_Man_\(song\) "Rocket Man (song)")" (1972), "[Kiss the Bride](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiss_the_Bride_\(song\) "Kiss the Bride (song)")" (1983), "[Sacrifice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sacrifice_\(Elton_John_song\) "Sacrifice (Elton John song)")" (1989) and "[Where's the Shoorah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_Moves "Blue Moves")?" (1976), the [remix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Remix "Remix") is an upbeat contemporary [synth-pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synth-pop "Synth-pop"), [dance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance_music "Dance music"), [dance-pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance-pop "Dance-pop") and [pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_music "Pop music") song describing the decline of a relationship.

"Cold Heart (Pnau remix)" reached the top position in the United Kingdom and marked Lipa's third and John's eighth chart-topping single on the [UK singles chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_singles_chart "UK singles chart"). The song achieved number one in the rankings of 12 other countries, including Australia, Canada and New Zealand. It also entered the top 10 in an additional 22 countries, including Ireland, South Africa and the United States. It peaked atop the Canadian [AC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_charts#Canadian_charts "Billboard charts"), CHR/Top 40 and Hot AC as well as the US [Adult Contemporary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adult_Contemporary_\(chart\) "Adult Contemporary (chart)"), [Adult Top 40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adult_Top_40 "Adult Top 40") and [Hot Dance/Electronic Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance/Electronic_Songs "Dance/Electronic Songs") rankings, respectively. The song received two gold and multiple platinum [certifications](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_recording_certification "Music recording certification") as well as two diamond awards from the [Syndicat National de l'Édition Phonographique](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syndicat_National_de_l'Édition_Phonographique "Syndicat National de l'Édition Phonographique") (SNEP) in France and the [Polish Society of the Phonographic Industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polish_Society_of_the_Phonographic_Industry "Polish Society of the Phonographic Industry") (ZPAV) in Poland, respectively. In 2022, it won an award in the category for the [Collaboration of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Music_Award_for_Collaboration_of_the_Year "American Music Award for Collaboration of the Year") at the [American Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Music_Awards_of_2022 "American Music Awards of 2022") and the [Top Dance/Electronic Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Music_Award_for_Top_Dance/Electronic_Song "Billboard Music Award for Top Dance/Electronic Song") at the [_Billboard_ Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Billboard_Music_Awards "2022 Billboard Music Awards").

"Cold Heart (Pnau remix)" was met with a warm reception from [music critics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_journalism "Music journalism") for its lyrics, sound and incorporation of John's four songs. Produced during the COVID-19 pandemic, the [animated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animation "Animation") [music video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_video "Music video") premiered on John's [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube") channel on 13 August 2021, with the aspiration of crafting a celebratory and joyful galaxy. It traces the adventure of John and Lipa together with four other animated characters as they explore the colorful and nature-filled psychedelic landscapes. An acoustic version and three additional remixes accompanied the song: renditions by [Claptone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claptone "Claptone"), PS1 and [The Blessed Madonna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Blessed_Madonna "The Blessed Madonna"). The song was further promoted with a live performance in Los Angeles on 20 November as part of John's [Farewell Yellow Brick Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farewell_Yellow_Brick_Road "Farewell Yellow Brick Road") tour, which was streamed on [Disney+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney+ "Disney+"). In 2022, it was ranked among the 10th most-streamed songs globally on [Apple Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Music "Apple Music") and [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify "Spotify").

## Background and development

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Cold_Heart_\(Pnau_remix\)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background and development")\]

Due to the outbreak of the [pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic") of [COVID-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19 "COVID-19"), John was compelled to temporarily halt his [Farewell Yellow Brick Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farewell_Yellow_Brick_Road "Farewell Yellow Brick Road") world tour in March 2020.[\[1\]](#cite_note-Krol-1) Amidst the [lockdown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_lockdowns "COVID-19 lockdowns") caused by the pandemic, the singer pursued a series of collaborations, one of which was "Cold Heart (Pnau remix)" with Lipa, as part of his upcoming studio album.[\[2\]](#cite_note-Daw-2)[\[3\]](#cite_note-Lavin-3) The album's songs were recorded over an 18-month period, either remotely through [Zoom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zoom_\(software\) "Zoom (software)") or in compliance with strict health and safety regulations.[\[2\]](#cite_note-Daw-2)[\[3\]](#cite_note-Lavin-3) Leading up to its release, John and Lipa previewed their collaborative effort by publishing cartoon representations of themselves, while dancing to a [disco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disco "Disco") melody on their respective [social media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_media "Social media") accounts on 10 August 2021.[\[4\]](#cite_note-Kenneally-4)[\[5\]](#cite_note-Mamo-5) The following day, the artists confirmed the song's title, "Cold Heart (Pnau remix)" and announced its release date set for 13 August.[\[6\]](#cite_note-6) The collaboration between the artists on the song was a testament to the friendship forged between the two, which was established through John's participation in Lipa's [Studio 2054](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Studio_2054 "Studio 2054") livestream in November 2020 and further strengthened by Lipa's performance at the [Elton John AIDS Foundation Academy Awards Viewing Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John_AIDS_Foundation_Academy_Award_Party "Elton John AIDS Foundation Academy Award Party") in August 2021.[\[7\]](#cite_note-Kenneally_13-7)[\[8\]](#cite_note-8)[\[9\]](#cite_note-9)[\[10\]](#cite_note-10) John stated, "\[Lipa has\] given me so much energy. She's a truly wonderful artist, and person, absolutely bursting with creativity and ideas. The energy she brought to \['the song'\] just blew my mind."[\[7\]](#cite_note-Kenneally_13-7) Lipa further added, "It has been an absolute honour and privilege to collaborate on this track with him. It's so very special \[...\] I loved being part of such a creative and joyous experience."[\[7\]](#cite_note-Kenneally_13-7)

![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/87/Gnome-mime-sound-openclipart.svg/60px-Gnome-mime-sound-openclipart.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)

A 16-second sample of "Cold Heart (Pnau Remix)", featuring an interpolation of [Elton John](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John "Elton John")'s single "[Rocket Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocket_Man_\(song\) "Rocket Man (song)")" (1972) with vocals from [Dua Lipa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dua_Lipa "Dua Lipa").[\[11\]](#cite_note-Walthall-11)

"Cold Heart (Pnau remix)" was written by John, Andrew Meecham, [Bernie Taupin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernie_Taupin "Bernie Taupin"), Dean Meredith, [Nicholas Littlemore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Littlemore "Nick Littlemore"), [Peter Mayes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Mayes "Peter Mayes") and [Sam Littlemore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Littlemore "Sam Littlemore"), with the production completed by the latter three, who form the group [Pnau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pnau "Pnau").[\[12\]](#cite_note-Spotify-12) The song has a duration time of three minutes and 22 seconds and was composed in the [time signature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_signature "Time signature") of **4**  
**4** and the [key](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Key_\(music\) "Key (music)") of [B-flat minor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B-flat_minor "B-flat minor"), with a [tempo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tempo "Tempo") of 116 beats per minute.[\[13\]](#cite_note-Release-13)[\[14\]](#cite_note-Musicnotes-14) The song is constructed in the [verse–chorus form](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Verse–chorus_form "Verse–chorus form") and uses the [chord progression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chord_progression "Chord progression") B♭m7–E♭m7–G♭-Fm7.[\[14\]](#cite_note-Musicnotes-14) The song was released for [digital download](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_download "Music download") and [streaming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Streaming_media "Streaming media") in various countries by [EMI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EMI_Records "EMI Records") and [Mercury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercury_Records "Mercury Records") on 13 August 2021 as the [lead single](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lead_single "Lead single") from John's 32nd studio album _[The Lockdown Sessions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Lockdown_Sessions_\(Elton_John_album\) "The Lockdown Sessions (Elton John album)")_ (2021).[\[13\]](#cite_note-Release-13) Paying homage to John's career, it [interpolates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interpolation_\(popular_music\) "Interpolation (popular music)") his songs "[Rocket Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocket_Man_\(song\) "Rocket Man (song)")" (1972), "[Kiss the Bride](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiss_the_Bride_\(song\) "Kiss the Bride (song)")" (1983), "[Sacrifice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sacrifice_\(Elton_John_song\) "Sacrifice (Elton John song)")" (1989) and "[Where's the Shoorah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_Moves "Blue Moves")?" (1976).[\[11\]](#cite_note-Walthall-11)[\[15\]](#cite_note-Legaspi-15)[\[16\]](#cite_note-Amter-16) The sample of "Where's the Shoorah?" appears at the 3:19 mark, with a tempo from 116 BPM to 130 BPM and a key shifted from an [E-flat major](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E-flat_major "E-flat major") to [B-flat minor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B-flat_minor "B-flat minor").[\[17\]](#cite_note-17) "Cold Heart (Pnau remix)" is an [upbeat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upbeat_\(music\) "Upbeat (music)"),[\[18\]](#cite_note-18) contemporary [synth-pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synth-pop "Synth-pop"),[\[19\]](#cite_note-Amsler-19) [dance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance_music "Dance music"), [dance-pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance-pop "Dance-pop") and [pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_music "Pop music") song,[\[20\]](#cite_note-Robledo-20)[\[21\]](#cite_note-Aniftos-21)[\[22\]](#cite_note-Chirilă-22) with [club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_dance_music "Electronic dance music"), disco and [house](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_music "House music") beats.[\[23\]](#cite_note-Rowley-23)[\[24\]](#cite_note-24) The lyrics transmit the [chorus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Refrain "Refrain") from "Rocket Man", which includes "And I think it's gonna be a long, long time 'til touchdown brings me 'round again to find / I'm not the man they think I am at home", and verses from "Sacrifice", such as "Cold, cold heart / hardened by you / Some things look better baby / Just passing through".[\[25\]](#cite_note-Aswad-25)[\[26\]](#cite_note-WRMF-26) They describe a relationship that has taken a turn for the worse due to the hardening of the singer's heart.[\[11\]](#cite_note-Walthall-11)

"Cold Heart (Pnau remix)" was met with a warm reception from [music critics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_journalism "Music journalism"), with many complimenting the combination of John's previous hits in the song. David Smyth from _[Evening Standard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evening_Standard "Evening Standard")_ characterised the song as a "particularly slick updating of classic Elton".[\[27\]](#cite_note-Smyth-27) [Annie Zaleski](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annie_Zaleski "Annie Zaleski") for _[Variety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety_\(magazine\) "Variety (magazine)")_ declared the result of the mashup to be "relentlessly modern, a seamless (and savvy) \[fusion\] of eras".[\[28\]](#cite_note-28) Althea Legaspi of _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ highlighted that the songs received a "[groove](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Groove_\(music\) "Groove (music)")\-tipped refresh" in the song.[\[15\]](#cite_note-Legaspi-15) Lars Brandle from _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")_ described the mashup as "expertly created".[\[29\]](#cite_note-Brandle-29) _Billboard_'s Stephen Daw thought that "Dua Lipa's voice sounds like butter as she croons the iconic chorus 'And I think it's gonna be a long, long time,' while the production from PNAU never goes over-the-top, only complementing John's original visions."[\[30\]](#cite_note-billboardreview-30) Helen Brown of _[The Independent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Independent "The Independent")_ wrote that the song "does a terrific job \[combining\] 'Sacrifice' and 'Rocket Man', giving both a [tendon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tendon "Tendon")\-twanging freshness".[\[31\]](#cite_note-31) Lakshmi Govindrajan Javeri from _[Firstpost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Firstpost "Firstpost")_ elaborated that the song "blends iconic portions of 'Sacrifice' and 'Rocket Man' to create a number that puritans will grudgingly admit is addictive at best, sacrilegious at worst".[\[32\]](#cite_note-32)

Emily Lee for [iHeart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IHeartRadio "IHeartRadio") commented that the mashup "may seem like a chaotic choice \[but\] Pnau \[...\] pull it together seamlessly".[\[33\]](#cite_note-33) Robert Moran for _[Sydney Morning Herald](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sydney_Morning_Herald "The Sydney Morning Herald")_ dubbed the song "ubiquitous", commending its blend of "Lipa's vocals on the hook and Pnau's atmospheric house sound and signature chants".[\[34\]](#cite_note-34) Daniela Avila of _[People](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People_\(magazine\) "People (magazine)")_ labeled the song as a "perfect dancefloor singalong".[\[35\]](#cite_note-35) Charlie Dukes from _[Renowned for Sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renowned_for_Sound "Renowned for Sound")_ marked the song as a "modern anthem" that "the world never knew it needed".[\[36\]](#cite_note-36) Gary Ryan for _[NME](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NME "NME")_ inscribed that the song "imperiously drapes itself over the [disco-revival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disco#2020s_resurgence "Disco") chaise longue".[\[37\]](#cite_note-37) Will Hodgkinson of _[The Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Times "The Times")_ wrote that the song "sounds cheesy as hell, yet the end result is so vibrant that you cannot help but be cheered by it".[\[38\]](#cite_note-38) Jordan Robledo from _[Gay Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gay_Times "Gay Times")_ praised John and Lipa's "incredible" vocal delivery that are "sure to leave fans yearning for their own trip to the dance floor".[\[20\]](#cite_note-Robledo-20) In conclusion, Jem Aswad for _Variety_ found the song "a living example of \[John's\] legendary patronage of younger artists and represents a new concept in mainstream musical reinvention".[\[25\]](#cite_note-Aswad-25) Terry Staunton of _[Record Collector](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Record_Collector "Record Collector")_ was less impressed, deriding it as "awkward" and "a little out of step".[\[39\]](#cite_note-39)

Some criticised the performance, such as The Mix Review, which commented it was boring and an excuse to cash in.[\[40\]](#cite_note-40)

In 2022, "Cold Heart (Pnau remix)" won an award in the category for the [Collaboration of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Music_Award_for_Collaboration_of_the_Year "American Music Award for Collaboration of the Year") at the [American Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Music_Awards_of_2022 "American Music Awards of 2022") and the [Top Dance/Electronic Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Music_Award_for_Top_Dance/Electronic_Song "Billboard Music Award for Top Dance/Electronic Song") at the [_Billboard_ Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Billboard_Music_Awards "2022 Billboard Music Awards").[\[41\]](#cite_note-41)[\[42\]](#cite_note-42) It was nominated for the [Song of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brit_Award_for_Song_of_the_Year "Brit Award for Song of the Year") at the [Brit Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brit_Awards_2022 "Brit Awards 2022"), the [Most Performed Work](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Ivor_Novello_Award_winners_and_nominees_\(2010s–2020s\) "List of Ivor Novello Award winners and nominees (2010s–2020s)") at the [Ivor Novello Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivor_Novello_Awards "Ivor Novello Awards") and the [Best Collaboration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Video_Music_Award_for_Best_Collaboration "MTV Video Music Award for Best Collaboration") and [Song of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Video_Music_Award_for_Song_of_the_Year "MTV Video Music Award for Song of the Year") at the [MTV Video Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_MTV_Video_Music_Awards "2022 MTV Video Music Awards").[\[43\]](#cite_note-43)[\[44\]](#cite_note-44)[\[45\]](#cite_note-45) In 2023, the song received nominations for the Best Collaboration and Dance Song of the Year at the [iHeartRadio Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_iHeartRadio_Music_Awards "2023 iHeartRadio Music Awards").[\[46\]](#cite_note-46) _Billboard_ and _[Los Angeles Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Times "Los Angeles Times")_ included "Cold Heart (Pnau remix)" in their year-end lists of the best songs for 2021.[\[47\]](#cite_note-47)[\[48\]](#cite_note-48) John and Lipa were further recognised as the "Hitmakers of the Year" by the American magazine _Variety_ in 2022, for the charting success of their collaboration on the charts.[\[25\]](#cite_note-Aswad-25)[\[49\]](#cite_note-49) During the summer of 2022, the song was ranked as the 19th most-streamed song on [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify "Spotify") worldwide.[\[50\]](#cite_note-50) On the year-end lists, it was ranked as the sixth and seventh most-streamed song on Spotify and [Apple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Music "Apple Music"), respectively.[\[51\]](#cite_note-51)[\[52\]](#cite_note-52)[\[53\]](#cite_note-Records-53) The song was also the most "shazamed" song of the year on [Shazam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shazam_\(music_app\) "Shazam (music app)") worldwide of that year.[\[53\]](#cite_note-Records-53)[\[54\]](#cite_note-54)

## Commercial performance

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Cold_Heart_\(Pnau_remix\)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Commercial performance")\]

In the United Kingdom, "Cold Heart (Pnau remix)" debuted at number 33 on the [UK singles chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_singles_chart "UK singles chart") in the issue dated 26 August 2021.[\[55\]](#cite_note-UK_Chart-55) The song reached number one, having spent three consecutive weeks at number two, with sales of 64,000, including 5.9 million streams and 5,000 copies on limited edition CD single, in its ninth week on the chart on 21 October.[\[55\]](#cite_note-UK_Chart-55)[\[56\]](#cite_note-United_Kingdom-56)[\[57\]](#cite_note-Ainsley-57) It represented Lipa's third chart-topping single in the UK, after "[New Rules](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Rules "New Rules")" (2017) and "[One Kiss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Kiss_\(song\) "One Kiss (song)")" (2018), and John's eighth and first in 16 years, since he was featured artist on American rapper [2Pac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tupac_Shakur "Tupac Shakur")'s posthumous single "[Ghetto Gospel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghetto_Gospel "Ghetto Gospel")" (2005).[\[57\]](#cite_note-Ainsley-57) John also became the first solo artist to achieve a top 10 single in six different decades, spanning from the [1970s](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1970s_in_music "1970s in music") to the [2020s](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020s_in_music "2020s in music").[\[58\]](#cite_note-58) In April 2023, the song received triple platinum certification from the [British Phonographic Industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Phonographic_Industry "British Phonographic Industry") (BPI) for shifting more than 1,800,000 units in the UK.[\[59\]](#cite_note-United_Kingdom_Cert-59) In Australia, "Cold Heart (Pnau remix)" reached number one on the [ARIA Singles Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ARIA_Charts "ARIA Charts") for 10 consecutive weeks as well as number one on the [New Zealand Singles Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Official_New_Zealand_Music_Chart "Official New Zealand Music Chart") in New Zealand.[\[60\]](#cite_note-Australia-60)[\[61\]](#cite_note-61)[\[62\]](#cite_note-New_Zealand-62) The song marked Lipa's first chart-topping single in Australia as well as John's first one since "[Something About the Way You Look Tonight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Something_About_the_Way_You_Look_Tonight "Something About the Way You Look Tonight")" / "[Candle in the Wind 1997](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Candle_in_the_Wind_1997 "Candle in the Wind 1997")" in 1997.[\[63\]](#cite_note-63) Also in 2022, it garnered a ten-times platinum certification from [Recorded Music New Zealand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recorded_Music_NZ "Recorded Music NZ") (RMNZ) in New Zealand for selling more than 300,000 units.[\[64\]](#cite_note-New_Zealand_Cert-64) In Australia, it was certified fifteen-times platinum by the [Australian Recording Industry Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Recording_Industry_Association "Australian Recording Industry Association") (ARIA) for selling 1,050,000 equivalent units.[\[65\]](#cite_note-Australia_Cert-65)

In Canada, "Cold Heart (Pnau remix)" reached number one on the [Canadian Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadian_Hot_100 "Canadian Hot 100") in the issue dated 8 January 2022, having spent a total of 12 consecutive weeks.[\[66\]](#cite_note-Canada-66)[\[67\]](#cite_note-67) The song also reached the top position on the [Canada AC, CHR/Top 40 and Hot AC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_charts#Canadian_charts "Billboard charts") rankings, respectively.[\[68\]](#cite_note-Canada_AC-68)[\[69\]](#cite_note-Canada_CHR-69)[\[70\]](#cite_note-Canada_HAC-70) In October 2022, it received a septuple platinum certification from [Music Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_Canada "Music Canada") (MC) for shifting more than 560,000 units in the Canada.[\[71\]](#cite_note-Canada_Cert-71) In the United States, "Cold Heart (Pnau remix)" entered the [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") at number 81 on 28 August 2021 and rose to number 32 in its fifth week, giving John the longest span of top 40 Hot 100 appearances, excluding holiday fare.[\[72\]](#cite_note-United_States-72)[\[73\]](#cite_note-73) The song reached its summit at number 7 on the ranking issue dated 15 January 2022, earning Lipa's fourth top 10 single on the chart and John's 28th entry.[\[72\]](#cite_note-United_States-72)[\[74\]](#cite_note-74) Topping the [Adult Contemporary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adult_Contemporary_\(chart\) "Adult Contemporary (chart)") and [Adult Top 40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adult_Top_40 "Adult Top 40") rankings,[\[75\]](#cite_note-BADC-75)[\[76\]](#cite_note-BADP-76) it further peaked at number one on the [Hot Dance/Electronic Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance/Electronic_Songs "Dance/Electronic Songs") chart, logging its 34th week at the top on 11 June.[\[77\]](#cite_note-BHDE-77)[\[78\]](#cite_note-78) In May 2022, the song garnered a double certification from the [Recording Industry Association of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recording_Industry_Association_of_America "Recording Industry Association of America") (RIAA) in the US for selling more than 2,000,000 units.[\[79\]](#cite_note-United_States_Cert-79)

"Cold Heart (Pnau remix)" reached the top position in Bulgaria,[\[80\]](#cite_note-Bulgaria-80) the [Commonwealth of Independent States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_of_Independent_States "Commonwealth of Independent States") (CIS),[\[81\]](#cite_note-CIS-81) Croatia,[\[82\]](#cite_note-Croatia-82) the Czech Republic,[\[83\]](#cite_note-Czech_Republic-83) Iceland,[\[84\]](#cite_note-Iceland-84) Lithuania,[\[85\]](#cite_note-Lithuania-85) Mexico,[\[86\]](#cite_note-Mexico-86) Poland, Ukraine and [Wallonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wallonia "Wallonia").[\[87\]](#cite_note-Poland-87)[\[88\]](#cite_note-Ukraine-88)[\[89\]](#cite_note-Wallonia-89) Top 10 positions were also achieved in Austria,[\[90\]](#cite_note-Austria-90) Costa Rica,[\[91\]](#cite_note-Costa_Rica-91) Denmark,[\[92\]](#cite_note-Denmark-92) El Salvador,[\[93\]](#cite_note-El_Salvador-93) [Flanders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flanders "Flanders"),[\[94\]](#cite_note-Flanders-94) France,[\[95\]](#cite_note-France-95) Germany,[\[96\]](#cite_note-Germany-96) Greece,[\[97\]](#cite_note-Greece-97) Hungary,[\[98\]](#cite_note-Hungary-98) Ireland,[\[99\]](#cite_note-Ireland-99) Italy,[\[100\]](#cite_note-Italy-100) Luxembourg,[\[101\]](#cite_note-Luxembourg-101) the Netherlands,[\[102\]](#cite_note-Netherlands-102) Norway,[\[103\]](#cite_note-Norway-103) Portugal,[\[104\]](#cite_note-Portugal-104) Romania,[\[105\]](#cite_note-Romania-105) Russia,[\[106\]](#cite_note-Russia-106) Slovakia,[\[107\]](#cite_note-Slovakia-107) South Africa,[\[108\]](#cite_note-South_Africa-108) Sweden, Switzerland and Uruguay.[\[109\]](#cite_note-Sweden-109)[\[110\]](#cite_no

"**Chemical**" is a song by American musician [Post Malone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone "Post Malone"). It was released through [Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_Records "Republic Records") and [Mercury Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercury_Records "Mercury Records") as the lead single from his fifth studio album, _[Austin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austin_\(album\) "Austin (album)")_, on April 14, 2023. The song was produced by Malone himself, [Andrew Watt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Watt_\(record_producer\) "Andrew Watt (record producer)"), and [Louis Bell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_Bell "Louis Bell"), and the three wrote it alongside Billy Walsh. One week after its release, the song appeared as the last track on Malone's first compilation album, _[The Diamond Collection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Diamond_Collection "The Diamond Collection")_, which was released to celebrate him becoming the artist with the most [diamond-certified](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RIAA_certification "RIAA certification") singles by the [Recording Industry Association of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recording_Industry_Association_of_America "Recording Industry Association of America") (RIAA), although the song was not certified at the time of the album's release.

In an early 2022 interview with _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")_ ahead of the release of his fourth studio album, _[Twelve Carat Toothache](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twelve_Carat_Toothache "Twelve Carat Toothache")_ (2022), Malone expressed plans to rebuild his artistic vision, even if that meant to compromise commercial success.[\[1\]](#cite_note-1) "Chemical" marks his first release as a lead artist since the album.[\[2\]](#cite_note-2) On April 12, 2023, Malone posted a clip of him listening to the song on his social media and announced the release.[\[3\]](#cite_note-Udiscover-3)

"Chemical" is a [pop rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_rock "Pop rock"), [soft rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soft_rock "Soft rock"), and [synth-pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synth-pop "Synth-pop") song that sees Malone return to his trademark sound,[\[4\]](#cite_note-4)[\[5\]](#cite_note-5)[\[6\]](#cite_note-6) while the song is also accompanied by an acoustic "folk-based" guitar and "contemporary pop elements".[\[7\]](#cite_note-hypebeast-7) It includes a "bright and catchy" chorus, which was described as a "contrast" to his previous moodier offerings. Despite the upbeat vibe of the chorus, the lyrical content was viewed as "on-brand" for Malone,[\[8\]](#cite_note-8) as he opens up about his inability to let go of a seemingly toxic relationship,[\[7\]](#cite_note-hypebeast-7) akin to an addiction.[\[9\]](#cite_note-9)

The accompanying official music video for "Chemical", directed by Alfred Marroquin, was released on April 14, 2023.[\[10\]](#cite_note-10) It sees Malone in different locations, including him smoking in a car like he says in the song as well as him dancing in front of a [beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beach "Beach"), [desert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desert "Desert"), [lightning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lightning "Lightning"), and [cloud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloud "Cloud") backdrop. In the beginning of the video he briefly walks by a [nighttime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nighttime "Nighttime") backdrop. The same backdrop can be seen at the very end of the video as he's seen sitting on top of a vehicle. In the beginning of the video and towards the middle of it, someone from behind the scenes can be seen pushing the backdrops, making way for a different backdrop. Malone also posted a lyric video, in which different angles are shown. The quality of the lyric video was reduced to create a [retro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retro "Retro") effect.[\[11\]](#cite_note-11)

"**Chemical**" is a song by American musician [Post Malone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone "Post Malone"). It was released through [Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_Records "Republic Records") and [Mercury Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercury_Records "Mercury Records") as the lead single from his fifth studio album, _[Austin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austin_\(album\) "Austin (album)")_, on April 14, 2023. The song was produced by Malone himself, [Andrew Watt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Watt_\(record_producer\) "Andrew Watt (record producer)"), and [Louis Bell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_Bell "Louis Bell"), and the three wrote it alongside Billy Walsh. One week after its release, the song appeared as the last track on Malone's first compilation album, _[The Diamond Collection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Diamond_Collection "The Diamond Collection")_, which was released to celebrate him becoming the artist with the most [diamond-certified](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RIAA_certification "RIAA certification") singles by the [Recording Industry Association of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recording_Industry_Association_of_America "Recording Industry Association of America") (RIAA), although the song was not certified at the time of the album's release.

In an early 2022 interview with _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")_ ahead of the release of his fourth studio album, _[Twelve Carat Toothache](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twelve_Carat_Toothache "Twelve Carat Toothache")_ (2022), Malone expressed plans to rebuild his artistic vision, even if that meant to compromise commercial success.[\[1\]](#cite_note-1) "Chemical" marks his first release as a lead artist since the album.[\[2\]](#cite_note-2) On April 12, 2023, Malone posted a clip of him listening to the song on his social media and announced the release.[\[3\]](#cite_note-Udiscover-3)

"Chemical" is a [pop rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_rock "Pop rock"), [soft rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soft_rock "Soft rock"), and [synth-pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synth-pop "Synth-pop") song that sees Malone return to his trademark sound,[\[4\]](#cite_note-4)[\[5\]](#cite_note-5)[\[6\]](#cite_note-6) while the song is also accompanied by an acoustic "folk-based" guitar and "contemporary pop elements".[\[7\]](#cite_note-hypebeast-7) It includes a "bright and catchy" chorus, which was described as a "contrast" to his previous moodier offerings. Despite the upbeat vibe of the chorus, the lyrical content was viewed as "on-brand" for Malone,[\[8\]](#cite_note-8) as he opens up about his inability to let go of a seemingly toxic relationship,[\[7\]](#cite_note-hypebeast-7) akin to an addiction.[\[9\]](#cite_note-9)

The accompanying official music video for "Chemical", directed by Alfred Marroquin, was released on April 14, 2023.[\[10\]](#cite_note-10) It sees Malone in different locations, including him smoking in a car like he says in the song as well as him dancing in front of a [beach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beach "Beach"), [desert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desert "Desert"), [lightning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lightning "Lightning"), and [cloud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloud "Cloud") backdrop. In the beginning of the video he briefly walks by a [nighttime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nighttime "Nighttime") backdrop. The same backdrop can be seen at the very end of the video as he's seen sitting on top of a vehicle. In the beginning of the video and towards the middle of it, someone from behind the scenes can be seen pushing the backdrops, making way for a different backdrop. Malone also posted a lyric video, in which different angles are shown. The quality of the lyric video was reduced to create a [retro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retro "Retro") effect.[\[11\]](#cite_note-11)

# Andrew Watt Defends Rolling Stones’ Grammy Win, Previews Lady Gaga’s ‘Mayhem’

Music Now

The producer goes deep on working with Gaga, the Rolling Stones, and other superstars in our career-spanning new interview

Producer/songwriter [Andrew Watt](https://www.rollingstone.com/t/andrew-watt/) went from the pop world to finding himself in the studio with his rock heroes, from the [Rolling Stones](https://www.rollingstone.com/t/rolling-stones/) to [Pearl Jam](https://www.rollingstone.com/t/pearl-jam/) — and now he’s back at the center of pop as executive producer of [Lady Gaga](https://www.rollingstone.com/t/lady-gaga/)‘s upcoming [album](https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/lady-gaga-mayhem-lyrics-album-preview-website-1235270520/) _Mayhem_. His career is reaching new heights at the moment, with a Grammy win for the Stones’ _Hackney Diamonds_, an Oscar nomination for a track with [Elton John](https://www.rollingstone.com/t/elton-john/) and Brandi Carlile (who have a Watt-produced dual album on the way), and a long run at Number One for Gaga and Bruno Mars’ “Die With A Smile.”  

In the new episode of _[Rolling Stone Music Now](https://www.rollingstone.com/t/rolling-stone-music-now/)_, Watt shares behind-the-scenes tales from his work with those superstars and much more. To hear the whole episode, go [here](https://link.chtbl.com/iw8-QbwN) for the podcast provider of your choice, listen on [Apple Podcasts](https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/rolling-stone-music-now/id1078431985) or [Spotify](https://open.spotify.com/show/0jCfnXfdYhwIM2I4x7SxZx), or just press play above. Here are some highlights from the discussion:

**Watt passionately defended the Stones’ recent Grammy win against online complaints that it slighted younger rock bands.** “They are in their eighties,” says Watt. “They’re 82 and 83 years old. Tell me another band ever in history that has made a latter-day album that good in their 80s, with that level of songwriting, that level of performance. Fuck the production —  I’m pressing record, you know what I mean? And making sure it sounds good. They’re playing, singing, writing, performing their asses off. You can’t tell me another band that has ever made an album in their 80s that is that good, and the reason you can’t tell me that is because rock and roll is not that old!…  It gives you faith in the human race, in what a human being could be capable of.” 

**Watt sees the rise of AI pushing pop music back toward human performances.** “It’s no coincidence that alongside all this live instrumentation is the rise of AI,” he says. “People are like, okay, computers are getting so good that they can kind of do this other stuff. What’s the realest, rawest thing that it _can’t_ do?” 

## Editor’s picks

**There are plenty of leftover songs from the _Hackney Diamonds_ sessions, and Watts wants the Stones to finish them.** “It was a prolific time for the band. Those sessions, they had amassed like 18 years of material,” Watt says. “There was so much to go through and there was so much to kind of choose from initially, and then there were new songs that just came because everyone was rolling and kind of flying. So we did record more than went onto the album…  There’s more material left. I can’t tell you if it’s gonna happen or not. It’s up to them, but it would be great… Why not finish the material, you know?”

**Gaga’s single “Abracadabra” came together spontaneously.** “She just heard something immediately, and grabbed the microphone and started flowing in the room,” says Watt. “Once there’s this initial kind of thing she always runs to the piano because then it becomes a song, and then what are the chords and there’s this crazy fun synth part and then where can it go… Once you came up with the chords for the other parts then we recorded that on other synths… You keep running between the control room and the live room, the control room and the live room.” 

**The making of “Die With a Smile” was as old-school as it gets.** “It was a really long day and night,” says Watt. “Bruno was there with \[producer/songwriter\] James Fauntleroy, and they just started playing together. Gaga wrote out all the chords and all the changing bass notes so she could know what she was going to play, Bruno was on the guitar, and they kind of just started breaking down the song together, really singing together and organically arranging their harmonies… Everything on that song is live. Live drums, live bass, live guitars, live vocals. Listen to them sing — it’s raw.”

**The upcoming final [Ozzy Osbourne concert](https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/black-sabbath-original-members-reunite-ozzy-osbourne-final-concert-1235257226/) will feature  “a zillion surprises,” Watt says.** “All I know is that I was asked to play in some concoction of things that they have put together. Ozzy is really excited for this concert. Anytime you give him a goal to hit or challenge, he’ll do it.”

**Watt has been quietly recording with [Paul McCartney](https://www.rollingstone.com/t/paul-mccartney/) between his other projects.** “He’s like my professor, Professor Paul,” says Watt. “We’ve been working on stuff in little chunks of time over the past couple of years. He also helped seal the deal for me in getting the Stones gig.”

# Andrew Watt Defends Rolling Stones’ Grammy Win, Previews Lady Gaga’s ‘Mayhem’

Music Now

The producer goes deep on working with Gaga, the Rolling Stones, and other superstars in our career-spanning new interview

Producer/songwriter [Andrew Watt](https://www.rollingstone.com/t/andrew-watt/) went from the pop world to finding himself in the studio with his rock heroes, from the [Rolling Stones](https://www.rollingstone.com/t/rolling-stones/) to [Pearl Jam](https://www.rollingstone.com/t/pearl-jam/) — and now he’s back at the center of pop as executive producer of [Lady Gaga](https://www.rollingstone.com/t/lady-gaga/)‘s upcoming [album](https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/lady-gaga-mayhem-lyrics-album-preview-website-1235270520/) _Mayhem_. His career is reaching new heights at the moment, with a Grammy win for the Stones’ _Hackney Diamonds_, an Oscar nomination for a track with [Elton John](https://www.rollingstone.com/t/elton-john/) and Brandi Carlile (who have a Watt-produced dual album on the way), and a long run at Number One for Gaga and Bruno Mars’ “Die With A Smile.”  

In the new episode of _[Rolling Stone Music Now](https://www.rollingstone.com/t/rolling-stone-music-now/)_, Watt shares behind-the-scenes tales from his work with those superstars and much more. To hear the whole episode, go [here](https://link.chtbl.com/iw8-QbwN) for the podcast provider of your choice, listen on [Apple Podcasts](https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/rolling-stone-music-now/id1078431985) or [Spotify](https://open.spotify.com/show/0jCfnXfdYhwIM2I4x7SxZx), or just press play above. Here are some highlights from the discussion:

**Watt passionately defended the Stones’ recent Grammy win against online complaints that it slighted younger rock bands.** “They are in their eighties,” says Watt. “They’re 82 and 83 years old. Tell me another band ever in history that has made a latter-day album that good in their 80s, with that level of songwriting, that level of performance. Fuck the production —  I’m pressing record, you know what I mean? And making sure it sounds good. They’re playing, singing, writing, performing their asses off. You can’t tell me another band that has ever made an album in their 80s that is that good, and the reason you can’t tell me that is because rock and roll is not that old!…  It gives you faith in the human race, in what a human being could be capable of.” 

**Watt sees the rise of AI pushing pop music back toward human performances.** “It’s no coincidence that alongside all this live instrumentation is the rise of AI,” he says. “People are like, okay, computers are getting so good that they can kind of do this other stuff. What’s the realest, rawest thing that it _can’t_ do?” 

## Editor’s picks

**There are plenty of leftover songs from the _Hackney Diamonds_ sessions, and Watts wants the Stones to finish them.** “It was a prolific time for the band. Those sessions, they had amassed like 18 years of material,” Watt says. “There was so much to go through and there was so much to kind of choose from initially, and then there were new songs that just came because everyone was rolling and kind of flying. So we did record more than went onto the album…  There’s more material left. I can’t tell you if it’s gonna happen or not. It’s up to them, but it would be great… Why not finish the material, you know?”

**Gaga’s single “Abracadabra” came together spontaneously.** “She just heard something immediately, and grabbed the microphone and started flowing in the room,” says Watt. “Once there’s this initial kind of thing she always runs to the piano because then it becomes a song, and then what are the chords and there’s this crazy fun synth part and then where can it go… Once you came up with the chords for the other parts then we recorded that on other synths… You keep running between the control room and the live room, the control room and the live room.” 

**The making of “Die With a Smile” was as old-school as it gets.** “It was a really long day and night,” says Watt. “Bruno was there with \[producer/songwriter\] James Fauntleroy, and they just started playing together. Gaga wrote out all the chords and all the changing bass notes so she could know what she was going to play, Bruno was on the guitar, and they kind of just started breaking down the song together, really singing together and organically arranging their harmonies… Everything on that song is live. Live drums, live bass, live guitars, live vocals. Listen to them sing — it’s raw.”

**The upcoming final [Ozzy Osbourne concert](https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/black-sabbath-original-members-reunite-ozzy-osbourne-final-concert-1235257226/) will feature  “a zillion surprises,” Watt says.** “All I know is that I was asked to play in some concoction of things that they have put together. Ozzy is really excited for this concert. Anytime you give him a goal to hit or challenge, he’ll do it.”

## Related Content

**Watt has been quietly recording with [Paul McCartney](https://www.rollingstone.com/t/paul-mccartney/) between his other projects.** “He’s like my professor, Professor Paul,” says Watt. “We’ve been working on stuff in little chunks of time over the past couple of years. He also helped seal the deal for me in getting the Stones gig.”

"**I Had Some Help**" is a song by American musician [Post Malone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone "Post Malone") featuring American [country music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_music "Country music") singer [Morgan Wallen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morgan_Wallen "Morgan Wallen"). It was released through [Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_Records "Republic Records") and [Mercury Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercury_Records "Mercury Records") as the [lead single](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lead_single "Lead single") from Malone's sixth studio album, _[F-1 Trillion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F-1_Trillion "F-1 Trillion")_, on May 10, 2024. They wrote the song with producers [Louis Bell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_Bell "Louis Bell"), [Charlie Handsome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlie_Handsome "Charlie Handsome"), and Hoskins, alongside [Ernest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernest_\(singer\) "Ernest (singer)"), [Ashley Gorley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashley_Gorley "Ashley Gorley"), and Chandler Paul Walters.

"I Had Some Help" received generally positive reviews from music critics. Commercially, the song debuted atop the [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") with the highest first week streams since 2020, giving Malone his sixth number one song and Wallen his second. It is the [second-longest running number one song of 2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Billboard_Hot_100_number_ones_of_2024 "List of Billboard Hot 100 number ones of 2024"), holding its position for six non consecutive weeks. It made history by debuting at number one on both the _Billboard_ Hot 100 and _Billboard_'s Hot Country Songs chart, and maintaining the top spot on each chart for its first five weeks, a feat that had never been achieved before. The song also debuted at number one on the _Billboard_'s annual Songs of the Summer chart and was subsequently crowned as the 2024 Song of the Summer at the end of the tracking period, having spent 14 weeks at the top. Additionally, it debuted and peaked atop the [_Billboard_ Global 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Global_200 "Billboard Global 200") chart and peaked at number one on the charts in Australia, Canada, Ireland, and Norway.

"I Had Some Help" has topped the US [Country Airplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_Airplay "Country Airplay") and the all format US [Radio Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radio_Songs_\(chart\) "Radio Songs (chart)") charts, making it the sixth song to achieve this milestone and the fastest to do so. It has also topped the US [Pop Airplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_Airplay "Pop Airplay") chart and also became Morgan Wallen's first [Adult Pop Airplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adult_Pop_Airplay "Adult Pop Airplay") number one hit.

On March 20, 2024, Malone previewed a snippet of the song through social media after a different snippet of a previous version leaked earlier, which had a problem with the mixing.[\[1\]](#cite_note-1) On May 2, 2024, the two artists took to social media to announce the title of the song and its release date.[\[2\]](#cite_note-2)

The song is written in the key of [C major](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C_major "C major"), with a [tempo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tempo "Tempo") of 128 [beats per minute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beats_per_minute "Beats per minute"), the main [chord progression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chord_progression "Chord progression") is F–C–Am–G.[\[3\]](#cite_note-3)[\[4\]](#cite_note-4)[\[5\]](#cite_note-5)

On May 10, 2024, Malone and Wallen released the official music video, which was filmed in Joshua Tree, California and directed by Chris Villa, with both artists playing leading roles. Also, starring Brandon Michaels as the Bouncer.[\[6\]](#cite_note-6)

## Commercial performance

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=I_Had_Some_Help&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Commercial performance")\]

"I Had Some Help" earned 167 first-week adds at country radio, making it only the second song in history to clear the panel in its first week after [Garth Brooks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garth_Brooks "Garth Brooks") in 1997 with "[Longneck Bottle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Longneck_Bottle "Longneck Bottle")".[\[7\]](#cite_note-Music_Row-7) It also broke [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify "Spotify")'s single-day country streaming record with nearly 14 million streams, debuted at No. 1 on the streaming platform's Global Daily chart and became its top male collaboration debut of all time, in addition to topping [Apple Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Music "Apple Music")'s Global chart and [Pandora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pandora_\(service\) "Pandora (service)")'s Top Thumb Hundred chart, upon release.[\[7\]](#cite_note-Music_Row-7)

In the United States, "I Had Some Help" debuted at number 18 on the _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")_ [Country Airplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_Airplay "Country Airplay") chart dated May 18, 2024, climbing to number nine the following week, before eventually reaching number one for the week June 29, 2024 after spending seven weeks on the chart. It is the first song to reach the top 10 in two weeks or fewer since Brooks' "[More Than a Memory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/More_Than_a_Memory "More Than a Memory")" debuted at number one in September 2007, as well as the fewest total cumulative weeks to reach number one since [Tim McGraw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_McGraw "Tim McGraw")'s "[Live Like You Were Dying](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Like_You_Were_Dying_\(song\) "Live Like You Were Dying (song)")" reached the top spot in its seventh week in July 2004. In addition, it is Malone's first number one on the Country Airplay chart, as well as Wallen's thirteenth.[\[8\]](#cite_note-8) The song would notch a second week at number one for the week of July 6, 2024 while Wallen's "[Cowgirls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowgirls_\(song\) "Cowgirls (song)")" featuring [Ernest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernest_\(singer\) "Ernest (singer)") held the number two position on the Country Airplay chart the same week, making Wallen the third artist in the chart's history to hold the top two positions concurrently.[\[9\]](#cite_note-9) It would remain at the top for two additional weeks before being displaced by "Cowgirls" on the chart dated July 27, 2024, making it the first time that an act has achieved back-to-back number one singles since 2002 when McGraw topped the chart back-to-back, first as a featured artist on [Jo Dee Messina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Dee_Messina "Jo Dee Messina")'s "[Bring On the Rain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bring_On_the_Rain "Bring On the Rain")" then with his own "[The Cowboy in Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Cowboy_in_Me "The Cowboy in Me")", and only the second time that such a distinction has been achieved in the chart's history.[\[10\]](#cite_note-10) The song currently ranks at No. 4 on the [Adult Pop Airplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adult_Pop_Airplay "Adult Pop Airplay") chart.[\[11\]](#cite_note-11)[\[12\]](#cite_note-12)[\[13\]](#cite_note-Billboard-13)

On the [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"), "I Had Some Help" debuted at number one on the chart dated May 25, 2024, with first-week figures of 76.4 million official streams, 31.1 million radio airplay audience impressions and 69,000 copies sold. It registered the highest first-week streaming figure since _Billboard_ removed [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube") song user-generated content from its chart metrics in year 2020, surpassing [Taylor Swift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift "Taylor Swift") and Post Malone's song "[Fortnight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortnight_\(song\) "Fortnight (song)")". It is Malone's sixth number-one single, fifth as lead artist, and second number-one debut. Post Malone tied the record as the fastest male artist to accumulate two No. 1 debuts on _Billboard_ Hot 100 history, "Fortnight" and "I Had Some Help" within just four weeks, after [Drake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\) "Drake (musician)") previously achieved the feat with the first two singles from his "[For All the Dogs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_All_the_Dogs "For All the Dogs")" album in 2023.[\[13\]](#cite_note-Billboard-13) "I Had Some Help" is the first song to spend its first five weeks on the _Billboard_ Hot 100 chart at No. 1 since [Miley Cyrus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miley_Cyrus "Miley Cyrus")' "[Flowers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flowers_\(Miley_Cyrus_song\) "Flowers (Miley Cyrus song)")", which held the top spot for its first six weeks in January–March 2023. It is also the first song in nearly a year to spend five consecutive weeks at No. 1 on the _Billboard_ Hot 100 chart, since Wallen's "[Last Night](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Last_Night_\(Morgan_Wallen_song\) "Last Night (Morgan Wallen song)")" spent 10 straight weeks at the top out of 16 total weeks in May–July 2023. Additionally, it is the first song to log six weeks at No. 1 on the _Billboard_ Hot 100 in 2024, surpassing the five weeks on top, of six total dating to late 2023, for [Jack Harlow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Harlow "Jack Harlow")'s "[Lovin on Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lovin_on_Me "Lovin on Me")".[\[14\]](#cite_note-Billboard3-14)[\[15\]](#cite_note-Billboard4-15) Furthermore, it is the first song to have debuted atop both the _Billboard_ Hot 100 and _Billboard_'s Hot Country Songs chart and spent its first five weeks on each at No. 1.[\[16\]](#cite_note-Billboard2-16)[\[14\]](#cite_note-Billboard3-14)

On the [_Billboard_ Global 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Global_200 "Billboard Global 200"), it debuted at No. 1 with 119 million streams and 81,000 sold worldwide in the week. It is the third Global 200 No. 1 that has topped _Billboard_'s Hot Country Songs chart, after [Beyoncé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beyoncé "Beyoncé")'s "[Texas Hold 'Em](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Hold_'Em_\(song\) "Texas Hold 'Em (song)")" and Taylor Swift's "[All Too Well (Taylor's Version)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well "All Too Well")."[\[17\]](#cite_note-17)

On the US [Radio Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radio_Songs_\(chart\) "Radio Songs (chart)") chart, "I Had Some Help" was the fastest song to hit the top five since [Miley Cyrus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miley_Cyrus "Miley Cyrus")' "[Flowers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flowers_\(Miley_Cyrus_song\) "Flowers (Miley Cyrus song)")" in 2023. It's also the first song to have reached the top five in as few as four weeks that has also hit the US Country Airplay chart's top five.[\[18\]](#cite_note-Bill-18) "I Had Some Help" became the sixth song and the fastest to do so, to top both the US Country Airplay and all-format US Radio Songs charts.[\[15\]](#cite_note-Billboard4-15)

The song debuted at number one on _Billboard_'s Annual Songs of the Summer chart and was subsequently crowned as the 2024 Song of the Summer at the end of the tracking period.[\[19\]](#cite_note-19)[\[14\]](#cite_note-Billboard3-14)[\[15\]](#cite_note-Billboard4-15)

The song was featured in the credits of the 2024 [Sony's Spider-Man Universe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony's_Spider-Man_Universe "Sony's Spider-Man Universe") film _[Venom: The Last Dance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venom:_The_Last_Dance "Venom: The Last Dance")_, used as a parallel for the toxic relationship between [Venom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venom_\(Sony's_Spider-Man_Universe\) "Venom (Sony's Spider-Man Universe)") and his symbiotic host [Eddie Brock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eddie_Brock_\(Sony's_Spider-Man_Universe\) "Eddie Brock (Sony's Spider-Man Universe)") ([Tom Hardy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Hardy "Tom Hardy")), even though the pair worked through it and ended up as best friends.[\[20\]](#cite_note-20)

On April 28, 2024, Malone and Wallen both performed their own sets at the [Stagecoach Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stagecoach_Festival "Stagecoach Festival") in Indio, California, and Wallen brought Malone out to perform the song with him for the first time ahead of its release.[\[29\]](#cite_note-29) On May 16, 2024, Malone performed the song at [59th Academy of Country Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/59th_Academy_of_Country_Music_Awards "59th Academy of Country Music Awards") in [Frisco, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frisco,_Texas "Frisco, Texas"). On May 28, 2024, Malone performed the song at [Louvre Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louvre_Museum "Louvre Museum") in [Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris "Paris").[\[30\]](#cite_note-30) On June 7, 2024, Malone performed the song at [Governor's Ball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governors_Ball_Music_Festival "Governors Ball Music Festival") in [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City").[\[31\]](#cite_note-31)

"**I Had Some Help**" is a song by American musician [Post Malone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_Malone "Post Malone") featuring American [country music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_music "Country music") singer [Morgan Wallen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morgan_Wallen "Morgan Wallen"). It was released through [Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_Records "Republic Records") and [Mercury Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercury_Records "Mercury Records") as the [lead single](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lead_single "Lead single") from Malone's sixth studio album, _[F-1 Trillion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F-1_Trillion "F-1 Trillion")_, on May 10, 2024. They wrote the song with producers [Louis Bell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_Bell "Louis Bell"), [Charlie Handsome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlie_Handsome "Charlie Handsome"), and Hoskins, alongside [Ernest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernest_\(singer\) "Ernest (singer)"), [Ashley Gorley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashley_Gorley "Ashley Gorley"), and Chandler Paul Walters.

"I Had Some Help" received generally positive reviews from music critics. Commercially, the song debuted atop the [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") with the highest first week streams since 2020, giving Malone his sixth number one song and Wallen his second. It is the [second-longest running number one song of 2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Billboard_Hot_100_number_ones_of_2024 "List of Billboard Hot 100 number ones of 2024"), holding its position for six non consecutive weeks. It made history by debuting at number one on both the _Billboard_ Hot 100 and _Billboard_'s Hot Country Songs chart, and maintaining the top spot on each chart for its first five weeks, a feat that had never been achieved before. The song also debuted at number one on the _Billboard_'s annual Songs of the Summer chart and was subsequently crowned as the 2024 Song of the Summer at the end of the tracking period, having spent 14 weeks at the top. Additionally, it debuted and peaked atop the [_Billboard_ Global 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Global_200 "Billboard Global 200") chart and peaked at number one on the charts in Australia, Canada, Ireland, and Norway.

"I Had Some Help" has topped the US [Country Airplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_Airplay "Country Airplay") and the all format US [Radio Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radio_Songs_\(chart\) "Radio Songs (chart)") charts, making it the sixth song to achieve this milestone and the fastest to do so. It has also topped the US [Pop Airplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_Airplay "Pop Airplay") chart and also became Morgan Wallen's first [Adult Pop Airplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adult_Pop_Airplay "Adult Pop Airplay") number one hit.

On March 20, 2024, Malone previewed a snippet of the song through social media after a different snippet of a previous version leaked earlier, which had a problem with the mixing.[\[1\]](#cite_note-1) On May 2, 2024, the two artists took to social media to announce the title of the song and its release date.[\[2\]](#cite_note-2)

The song is written in the key of [C major](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C_major "C major"), with a [tempo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tempo "Tempo") of 128 [beats per minute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beats_per_minute "Beats per minute"), the main [chord progression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chord_progression "Chord progression") is F–C–Am–G.[\[3\]](#cite_note-3)[\[4\]](#cite_note-4)[\[5\]](#cite_note-5)

On May 10, 2024, Malone and Wallen released the official music video, which was filmed in Joshua Tree, California and directed by Chris Villa, with both artists playing leading roles. Also, starring Brandon Michaels as the Bouncer.[\[6\]](#cite_note-6)

## Commercial performance

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=I_Had_Some_Help&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Commercial performance")\]

"I Had Some Help" earned 167 first-week adds at country radio, making it only the second song in history to clear the panel in its first week after [Garth Brooks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garth_Brooks "Garth Brooks") in 1997 with "[Longneck Bottle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Longneck_Bottle "Longneck Bottle")".[\[7\]](#cite_note-Music_Row-7) It also broke [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify "Spotify")'s single-day country streaming record with nearly 14 million streams, debuted at No. 1 on the streaming platform's Global Daily chart and became its top male collaboration debut of all time, in addition to topping [Apple Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Music "Apple Music")'s Global chart and [Pandora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pandora_\(service\) "Pandora (service)")'s Top Thumb Hundred chart, upon release.[\[7\]](#cite_note-Music_Row-7)

In the United States, "I Had Some Help" debuted at number 18 on the _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_\(magazine\) "Billboard (magazine)")_ [Country Airplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_Airplay "Country Airplay") chart dated May 18, 2024, climbing to number nine the following week, before eventually reaching number one for the week June 29, 2024 after spending seven weeks on the chart. It is the first song to reach the top 10 in two weeks or fewer since Brooks' "[More Than a Memory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/More_Than_a_Memory "More Than a Memory")" debuted at number one in September 2007, as well as the fewest total cumulative weeks to reach number one since [Tim McGraw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_McGraw "Tim McGraw")'s "[Live Like You Were Dying](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_Like_You_Were_Dying_\(song\) "Live Like You Were Dying (song)")" reached the top spot in its seventh week in July 2004. In addition, it is Malone's first number one on the Country Airplay chart, as well as Wallen's thirteenth.[\[8\]](#cite_note-8) The song would notch a second week at number one for the week of July 6, 2024 while Wallen's "[Cowgirls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cowgirls_\(song\) "Cowgirls (song)")" featuring [Ernest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernest_\(singer\) "Ernest (singer)") held the number two position on the Country Airplay chart the same week, making Wallen the third artist in the chart's history to hold the top two positions concurrently.[\[9\]](#cite_note-9) It would remain at the top for two additional weeks before being displaced by "Cowgirls" on the chart dated July 27, 2024, making it the first time that an act has achieved back-to-back number one singles since 2002 when McGraw topped the chart back-to-back, first as a featured artist on [Jo Dee Messina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Dee_Messina "Jo Dee Messina")'s "[Bring On the Rain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bring_On_the_Rain "Bring On the Rain")" then with his own "[The Cowboy in Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Cowboy_in_Me "The Cowboy in Me")", and only the second time that such a distinction has been achieved in the chart's history.[\[10\]](#cite_note-10) The song currently ranks at No. 4 on the [Adult Pop Airplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adult_Pop_Airplay "Adult Pop Airplay") chart.[\[11\]](#cite_note-11)[\[12\]](#cite_note-12)[\[13\]](#cite_note-Billboard-13)

On the [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"), "I Had Some Help" debuted at number one on the chart dated May 25, 2024, with first-week figures of 76.4 million official streams, 31.1 million radio airplay audience impressions and 69,000 copies sold. It registered the highest first-week streaming figure since _Billboard_ removed [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube") song user-generated content from its chart metrics in year 2020, surpassing [Taylor Swift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift "Taylor Swift") and Post Malone's song "[Fortnight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortnight_\(song\) "Fortnight (song)")". It is Malone's sixth number-one single, fifth as lead artist, and second number-one debut. Post Malone tied the record as the fastest male artist to accumulate two No. 1 debuts on _Billboard_ Hot 100 history, "Fortnight" and "I Had Some Help" within just four weeks, after [Drake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drake_\(musician\) "Drake (musician)") previously achieved the feat with the first two singles from his "[For All the Dogs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_All_the_Dogs "For All the Dogs")" album in 2023.[\[13\]](#cite_note-Billboard-13) "I Had Some Help" is the first song to spend its first five weeks on the _Billboard_ Hot 100 chart at No. 1 since [Miley Cyrus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miley_Cyrus "Miley Cyrus")' "[Flowers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flowers_\(Miley_Cyrus_song\) "Flowers (Miley Cyrus song)")", which held the top spot for its first six weeks in January–March 2023. It is also the first song in nearly a year to spend five consecutive weeks at No. 1 on the _Billboard_ Hot 100 chart, since Wallen's "[Last Night](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Last_Night_\(Morgan_Wallen_song\) "Last Night (Morgan Wallen song)")" spent 10 straight weeks at the top out of 16 total weeks in May–July 2023. Additionally, it is the first song to log six weeks at No. 1 on the _Billboard_ Hot 100 in 2024, surpassing the five weeks on top, of six total dating to late 2023, for [Jack Harlow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Harlow "Jack Harlow")'s "[Lovin on Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lovin_on_Me "Lovin on Me")".[\[14\]](#cite_note-Billboard3-14)[\[15\]](#cite_note-Billboard4-15) Furthermore, it is the first song to have debuted atop both the _Billboard_ Hot 100 and _Billboard_'s Hot Country Songs chart and spent its first five weeks on each at No. 1.[\[16\]](#cite_note-Billboard2-16)[\[14\]](#cite_note-Billboard3-14)

On the [_Billboard_ Global 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Global_200 "Billboard Global 200"), it debuted at No. 1 with 119 million streams and 81,000 sold worldwide in the week. It is the third Global 200 No. 1 that has topped _Billboard_'s Hot Country Songs chart, after [Beyoncé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beyoncé "Beyoncé")'s "[Texas Hold 'Em](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Hold_'Em_\(song\) "Texas Hold 'Em (song)")" and Taylor Swift's "[All Too Well (Taylor's Version)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Too_Well "All Too Well")."[\[17\]](#cite_note-17)

On the US [Radio Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radio_Songs_\(chart\) "Radio Songs (chart)") chart, "I Had Some Help" was the fastest song to hit the top five since [Miley Cyrus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miley_Cyrus "Miley Cyrus")' "[Flowers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flowers_\(Miley_Cyrus_song\) "Flowers (Miley Cyrus song)")" in 2023. It's also the first song to have reached the top five in as few as four weeks that has also hit the US Country Airplay chart's top five.[\[18\]](#cite_note-Bill-18) "I Had Some Help" became the sixth song and the fastest to do so, to top both the US Country Airplay and all-format US Radio Songs charts.[\[15\]](#cite_note-Billboard4-15)

The song debuted at number one on _Billboard_'s Annual Songs of the Summer chart and was subsequently crowned as the 2024 Song of the Summer at the end of the tracking period.[\[19\]](#cite_note-19)[\[14\]](#cite_note-Billboard3-14)[\[15\]](#cite_note-Billboard4-15)

The song was featured in the credits of the 2024 [Sony's Spider-Man Universe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony's_Spider-Man_Universe "Sony's Spider-Man Universe") film _[Venom: The Last Dance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venom:_The_Last_Dance "Venom: The Last Dance")_, used as a parallel for the toxic relationship between [Venom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venom_\(Sony's_Spider-Man_Universe\) "Venom (Sony's Spider-Man Universe)") and his symbiotic host [Eddie Brock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eddie_Brock_\(Sony's_Spider-Man_Universe\) "Eddie Brock (Sony's Spider-Man Universe)") ([Tom Hardy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Hardy "Tom Hardy")), even though the pair worked through it and ended up as best friends.[\[20\]](#cite_note-20)

On April 28, 2024, Malone and Wallen both performed their own sets at the [Stagecoach Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stagecoach_Festival "Stagecoach Festival") in Indio, California, and Wallen brought Malone out to perform the song with him for the first time ahead of its release.[\[29\]](#cite_note-29) On May 16, 2024, Malone performed the song at [59th Academy of Country Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/59th_Academy_of_Country_Music_Awards "59th Academy of Country Music Awards") in [Frisco, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frisco,_Texas "Frisco, Texas"). On May 28, 2024, Malone performed the song at [Louvre Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louvre_Museum "Louvre Museum") in [Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris "Paris").[\[30\]](#cite_note-30) On June 7, 2024, Malone performed the song at [Governor's Ball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governors_Ball_Music_Festival "Governors Ball Music Festival") in [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City").[\[31\]](#cite_note-31)
