_**The Lockdown Sessions**_ is a collaborative studio album by British musician [Elton John](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elton_John "Elton John"), released through [EMI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EMI_Records "EMI Records") in the United Kingdom and [Interscope Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interscope_Records "Interscope Records") in the United States on 22 October 2021.[\[1\]](#cite_note-Rolling_Stone-1) It was recorded during the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_the_United_Kingdom "COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom"), after John was forced to pause his [Farewell Yellow Brick Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farewell_Yellow_Brick_Road "Farewell Yellow Brick Road") tour due to [lockdown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_lockdowns "COVID-19 lockdowns").[\[2\]](#cite_note-2) The album includes three singles: "[Cold Heart (Pnau remix)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_Heart_\(Pnau_remix\) "Cold Heart (Pnau remix)")" with [Dua Lipa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dua_Lipa "Dua Lipa"), "After All" with [Charlie Puth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlie_Puth "Charlie Puth"), and "Finish Line" with [Stevie Wonder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stevie_Wonder "Stevie Wonder"). A 2022 reissue of the album includes "[Merry Christmas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Merry_Christmas_\(song\) "Merry Christmas (song)")" with [Ed Sheeran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ed_Sheeran "Ed Sheeran") and "[Hold Me Closer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hold_Me_Closer_\(Elton_John_and_Britney_Spears_song\) "Hold Me Closer (Elton John and Britney Spears song)")" with [Britney Spears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Britney_Spears "Britney Spears").

_The Lockdown Sessions_ was a critical and commercial success, being praised for its performances and diversity. "Cold Heart (Pnau remix)" topped the [UK singles chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_singles_chart "UK singles chart") while "Hold Me Closer" reached number three; both singles also reached the top 10 in the US.

The album features several previously released tracks: "[Learn to Fly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Learn_to_Fly_\(Surfaces_and_Elton_John_song\) "Learn to Fly (Surfaces and Elton John song)")", released in June 2020; "Chosen Family", John's duet with [Rina Sawayama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rina_Sawayama "Rina Sawayama") on her _[Sawayama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sawayama "Sawayama")_ album;[\[3\]](#cite_note-Billboard-3) [Gorillaz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gorillaz "Gorillaz")' track "[The Pink Phantom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Pink_Phantom "The Pink Phantom")" from their 2020 album _[Song Machine, Season One: Strange Timez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Song_Machine,_Season_One:_Strange_Timez "Song Machine, Season One: Strange Timez")_, on which John appears as a guest alongside [6lack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/6lack "6lack"); John's cover of the [Pet Shop Boys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pet_Shop_Boys "Pet Shop Boys")' "[It's a Sin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It's_a_Sin "It's a Sin")" along with [Years & Years](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Years_&_Years "Years & Years"), released in May 2021;[\[3\]](#cite_note-Billboard-3) [Miley Cyrus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miley_Cyrus "Miley Cyrus")' version of "[Nothing Else Matters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nothing_Else_Matters "Nothing Else Matters")" featuring John alongside various other guests (including [Andrew Watt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Watt "Andrew Watt"), [Yo-Yo Ma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yo-Yo_Ma "Yo-Yo Ma"), [Robert Trujillo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Trujillo "Robert Trujillo") and [Chad Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chad_Smith "Chad Smith")), released in June 2021 from the [Metallica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metallica "Metallica") [tribute album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tribute_album "Tribute album") _[The Metallica Blacklist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Metallica_Blacklist "The Metallica Blacklist")_; and John's collaboration with [Lil Nas X](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Nas_X "Lil Nas X") "One of Me", from Lil Nas X's debut studio album _[Montero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montero_\(album\) "Montero (album)")_.

Besides these, the record also features collaborations with other artists including [Pearl Jam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pearl_Jam "Pearl Jam") frontman [Eddie Vedder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eddie_Vedder "Eddie Vedder"), [Brandi Carlile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brandi_Carlile "Brandi Carlile"), [Charlie Puth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlie_Puth "Charlie Puth"), [Stevie Wonder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stevie_Wonder "Stevie Wonder"), [Nicki Minaj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicki_Minaj "Nicki Minaj"), [Young Thug](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Young_Thug "Young Thug"), [Stevie Nicks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stevie_Nicks "Stevie Nicks"), and [Glen Campbell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glen_Campbell "Glen Campbell").[\[4\]](#cite_note-4)[\[5\]](#cite_note-5)[\[3\]](#cite_note-Billboard-3)

John explained the project in a statement: "Some of the recording sessions had to be done remotely, via [Zoom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zoom_\(software\) "Zoom (software)"), which I'd obviously never done before. Some of the sessions were recorded under very stringent safety regulations: working with another artist, but separated by glass screens. But all the tracks I worked on were really interesting and diverse, stuff that was completely different to anything I'm known for, stuff that took me out of my comfort zone into completely new territory. And I realised there was something weirdly familiar about working like this. At the start of my career, in the late 60s, I worked as a [session musician](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Session_musician "Session musician"). Working with different artists during lockdown reminded me of that. I'd come full circle: I was a session musician again. And it was still a blast."[\[6\]](#cite_note-6)

When talking about his collaboration with [Surfaces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surfaces_\(band\) "Surfaces (band)") on the song "Learn to Fly", John [tweeted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tweeted "Tweeted"): "When the guys first sent me the song, I just loved it. It was an honour to lend my vocals and some piano."[\[7\]](#cite_note-7) In a statement, Surfaces said: "After a series of Zoom studio sessions, we were able to record together from [quarantine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"). Working with Elton felt like the idea of winning a [Grammy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy "Grammy"). He was so passionate and driven and we couldn't have wished for a more effortless collaboration."[\[8\]](#cite_note-8) A music video to accompany the release of "Learn to Fly" was released onto [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube") on 24 June 2020.[\[9\]](#cite_note-9) It was made in collaboration with director and illustrator Ivan Dixon, who also provided the visuals for Surfaces' song "Bloom", and was produced by Sean Zwan from Studio Showoff.[\[10\]](#cite_note-10)

When the album hit number-one in the [UK Albums Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Albums_Chart "UK Albums Chart") on 29 October 2021, John said "I am so proud of what we have created"[\[11\]](#cite_note-11) and wrote on his social media accounts:

> "This album is all about the capacity for music to bring people together to form new friendships and connections and right now I couldn't feel more connected to my amazing fans in the UK who made this happen.
> 
> When I started collaborating with some of my favourite artists at the start of the pandemic, I couldn't have dreamt in my wildest dreams it would lead to a number one album. I am so proud of what we have created and thrilled that it has connected with our fans to such a degree. It shows the spirit of collaboration and togetherness that can still happen in the most trying circumstances.
> 
> Thank you to everyone who helped bring this album to life—I love you all. ❤"

— Elton John[\[12\]](#cite_note-12)

The lead single, "[Cold Heart (Pnau remix)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_Heart_\(Pnau_remix\) "Cold Heart (Pnau remix)")" with [Dua Lipa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dua_Lipa "Dua Lipa"), combines elements of John's 1989 song "[Sacrifice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sacrifice_\(Elton_John_song\) "Sacrifice (Elton John song)")", his 1972 single "[Rocket Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocket_Man_\(song\) "Rocket Man (song)")", his 1976 album track "Where's the Shoorah?" from _[Blue Moves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_Moves "Blue Moves")_ and his 1983 single "[Kiss the Bride](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiss_the_Bride_\(song\) "Kiss the Bride (song)")", and was released on 13 August 2021. On 15 October 2021, the single peaked at number one on the [UK singles chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_singles_chart "UK singles chart"). This was John's first UK number one in 16 years, since 2005's posthumous [Tupac Shakur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tupac_Shakur "Tupac Shakur") collaboration "[Ghetto Gospel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghetto_Gospel "Ghetto Gospel")".[\[13\]](#cite_note-13)

The album's official second single, "After All", is a collaboration with American singer Charlie Puth. It was released on 22 September 2021.[\[14\]](#cite_note-14)[\[15\]](#cite_note-15)[\[16\]](#cite_note-16)

The album's official third single, "Finish Line", is a collaboration with American singer Stevie Wonder. It was released on 30 September 2021.[\[17\]](#cite_note-17)[\[18\]](#cite_note-18) "Finish Line" failed to chart on the Official UK Top 100, but debuted at number 73 on the Official UK Singles Sales Chart Top 100 on 28 January 2022[\[19\]](#cite_note-19)

"Pour Me a Drink" is a [country pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_pop "Country pop") song.[\[1\]](#cite_note-1)

On May 24, 2024, Malone previewed a snippet of the song through social media. On June 13, Malone announced that a single, "Pour Me a Drink" featuring Shelton, would be released on June 21.[\[2\]](#cite_note-2)[\[3\]](#cite_note-3)

["Abracadabra"](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vBynw9Isr28) on [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube_video_\(identifier\) "YouTube video (identifier)")

"**Abracadabra**" is a song recorded by American singer-songwriter [Lady Gaga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lady_Gaga "Lady Gaga") for her studio album, _[Mayhem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayhem_\(Lady_Gaga_album\) "Mayhem (Lady Gaga album)")_ (2025). It was written and produced by Gaga, [Andrew Watt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Watt "Andrew Watt"), and [Cirkut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cirkut "Cirkut"), with additional songwriting credits to members of [Siouxsie and the Banshees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siouxsie_and_the_Banshees "Siouxsie and the Banshees"), as it incorporates elements from their 1981 single "[Spellbound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spellbound_\(Siouxsie_and_the_Banshees_song\) "Spellbound (Siouxsie and the Banshees song)")". Musically, it is a [dance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance_music "Dance music"), [dance-pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance-pop "Dance-pop"), [electropop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electropop "Electropop"), [synth-pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synth-pop "Synth-pop"), and [acid techno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acid_techno "Acid techno") track with [electronic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_music "Electronic music"), [industrial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Industrial_music "Industrial music"), [house](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_music "House music"), and [psychedelic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychedelic_music "Psychedelic music") influences. The song's lyrics, according to Gaga, reflect on facing life's challenges and finding a sense of magic in them. "Abracadabra" was released through [Interscope Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interscope_Records "Interscope Records") on February 3, 2025, as the album's second single.

An accompanying music video, co-directed by Gaga, [Parris Goebel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parris_Goebel "Parris Goebel"), and Bethany Vargas, depicts a dance battle between two contrasting personas of the singer and premiered on February 3, following a teaser which aired during a commercial break at the [67th Annual Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/67th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "67th Annual Grammy Awards"). Critics praised its theatrical style and cinematography, drawing favorable comparisons to her earlier work. Gaga performed "Abracadabra" on _[Saturday Night Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saturday_Night_Live "Saturday Night Live")_, _[The Howard Stern Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Howard_Stern_Show "The Howard Stern Show")_, the [MTV Video Music Awards 2025](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_MTV_Video_Music_Awards "2025 MTV Video Music Awards") and the 2026 Grammy Awards. She also sang it as part of the opening act for [some concerts promoting _Mayhem_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayhem_promotional_concerts "Mayhem promotional concerts"), including during [the Mayhem Ball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Mayhem_Ball "The Mayhem Ball") tour, and incorporated a remix of the track by French producer [Gesaffelstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gesaffelstein "Gesaffelstein") as a show interlude, which was released on digital platforms. Gaga also performed a reimagined version of the song for _[Mayhem Requiem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Music_Live:_Mayhem_Requiem "Apple Music Live: Mayhem Requiem")_.

"Abracadabra" received critical acclaim, with reviewers praising its production, rhythm, songwriting and chorus, and various critics ranked it among the best songs of 2025. Commercially, the song topped the charts in Hungary and Lithuania, while reaching the top ten in Austria, Brazil, Croatia, Finland, Germany, Ireland, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Portugal, Singapore, Sweden, Switzerland, the United Kingdom, and on the [_Billboard_ Global 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Global_200 "Billboard Global 200"). "Abracadabra" also charted within the top twenty in Australia, Belgium, Canada, Costa Rica, France, New Zealand, the Philippines, Taiwan, the United Arab Emirates, and the United States. It also received diamond certifications in Brazil and France as well as platinum certifications in Australia, Austria, Belgium, Canada, the Czech Republic, Greece, New Zealand, Poland, Portugal, Slovakia, and the United Kingdom. At the [68th Annual Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/68th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "68th Annual Grammy Awards"), "Abracadabra" was nominated for [Record of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Record_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Record of the Year"), [Song of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Song_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Song of the Year"), [Best Dance Pop Recording](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Dance_Pop_Recording "Grammy Award for Best Dance Pop Recording"), and—for its Gesaffelstein remix—[Best Remixed Recording, Non-Classical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Remixed_Recording,_Non-Classical "Grammy Award for Best Remixed Recording, Non-Classical"), winning the latter two.

6/10[\[30\]](#cite_note-uncut-30)

_The Lockdown Sessions_ received generally positive reviews from music critics. According to the review aggregator [Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic"), _The Lockdown Sessions_ received "generally favorable reviews" based on a [weighted average](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weighted_arithmetic_mean "Weighted arithmetic mean") score of 70 out of 100 from 10 critic scores.[\[21\]](#cite_note-Metacritic-21) Aggregator AnyDecentMusic? gave it 6.8 out of 10, based on their assessment of the critical consensus.[\[20\]](#cite_note-AnyDecentMusic?-20)

[Stephen Thomas Erlewine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Thomas_Erlewine "Stephen Thomas Erlewine") of [AllMusic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AllMusic "AllMusic") said, "The record is at its best when it's close to an old-fashioned duet album."[\[22\]](#cite_note-allmusic-22) Helen Brown of _[The Independent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Independent "The Independent")_ said, "There are a couple of stunning vocal performances. Rina Sawayama sings like a galleon in full sail on the big, bold ballad "Chosen Family". ... Grim moments include Young Thug's sleazy sex rap on "I Will Always Love You." ... In the middle ground are a few hummable collaborations ("Learn to Fly" with Surfaces, "Finish Line" with Stevie Wonder)."[\[23\]](#cite_note-theindependent-23) John Aizlewood of _[Mojo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mojo_\(magazine\) "Mojo (magazine)")_ said, "Probably his most varied album. ... The extremes work better still, be it Cyrus's eyebrow-raising raw trawl through Metallica's Nothing Else Matters or the vocal pyrotechnics which course through Young Thug & Nicki Minaj's Always Love You."[\[24\]](#cite_note-mojo-24) John Murphy of _[MusicOMH](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MusicOMH "MusicOMH")_ called the album "an album that could have easily come off as a millionaire's vanity project with his rich mates is actually a surprising, creatively rich endeavour."[\[25\]](#cite_note-musicomh-25) Gary Ryan of _[NME](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NME "NME")_ said, "All in all, _The Lockdown Sessions_ all-bets-off stylistic game of spin-the-bottle feels attuned to 2021's post-genre Spotify world, as Elton continues to further his musical universe. The Rocketman remains in orbit."[\[26\]](#cite_note-nme-26) Kate Hutchinson of _[The Observer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Observer "The Observer")_ said, "It's all fun, though a little disjointed – and the less said about Elton's trap song, Always Love You, with Nicki Minaj and Young Thug, the better."[\[27\]](#cite_note-theobserver-27) Rich Wilhelm of _[PopMatters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PopMatters "PopMatters")_ said, "_The Lockdown Sessions_ is an engaging series of snapshots of time well-spent."[\[28\]](#cite_note-popmatters-28) Jon Dolan of _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ said, "Even if this project probably won't give us any fresh entrants into the large canon of classic Elton songs, _The Lockdown Sessions_ is still a glowing testament to his enduring pop gravitas."[\[29\]](#cite_note-rollingstone-29) Stephen Troussé of _[Uncut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uncut_\(magazine\) "Uncut (magazine)")_ called the album "a rum selection of Zoom collaborations with everyone from Dua Lipa to Lil Nas X, that old keenness is still there, though only on "It's a Sin," his Brits team-up with Olly Alexander."[\[30\]](#cite_note-uncut-30) Annie Zaleski of _[Variety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety_\(magazine\) "Variety (magazine)")_ said, "John's open-hearted vocals and sincerity make _The Lockdown Sessions_ a charming listen."[\[31\]](#cite_note-31)

## Commercial performance

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=The_Lockdown_Sessions_\(Elton_John_album\)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Commercial performance")\]

The album was released on 22 October 2021, and in the [OCC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Official_Charts_Company "Official Charts Company")'s UK midweek chart update on 25 October, the album was described as being in a "four way battle" with [Duran Duran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duran_Duran "Duran Duran")'s _[Future Past](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Future_Past_\(Duran_Duran_album\) "Future Past (Duran Duran album)")_, [Lana Del Rey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lana_Del_Rey "Lana Del Rey")'s _[Blue Banisters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_Banisters "Blue Banisters")_ and [Biffy Clyro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biffy_Clyro "Biffy Clyro")'s _[The Myth of the Happily Ever After](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Myth_of_the_Happily_Ever_After "The Myth of the Happily Ever After")_ for the number-one position.[\[32\]](#cite_note-32) It later became John's eighth number-one album in the UK on 29 October 2021, his first number-one album since 2012's _[Good Morning to the Night](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Good_Morning_to_the_Night "Good Morning to the Night")_.[\[33\]](#cite_note-33)

_The Lockdown Sessions_ achieved 31,000 chart sales in the UK, 84% of which were physical (CD and vinyl) sales in the first week. It was John's second number one in the UK in less than a month – "Cold Heart (Pnau remix)" with Dua Lipa reached number one on the UK Singles Chart earlier in the month.[\[34\]](#cite_note-34) In the United States, the album debuted at number ten on the [_Billboard_ 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200 "Billboard 200") with first-week sales of 29,000 album-equivalent units, 17,000 of that sum were pure album copies, it went straight to number four on the U.S. [Top Album Sales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Top_Album_Sales "Top Album Sales") chart.[\[35\]](#cite_note-35)[\[36\]](#cite_note-36)

The extremes work better still, be it Cyrus's eyebrow-raising raw trawl through Metallica's Nothing Else Matters or the vocal pyrotechnics which course through Young Thug & Nicki Minaj's Always Love You."[\[24\]](#cite_note-mojo-24) John Murphy of _[MusicOMH](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MusicOMH "MusicOMH")_ called the album "an album that could have easily come off as a millionaire's vanity project with his rich mates is actually a surprising, creatively rich endeavour."[\[25\]](#cite_note-musicomh-25) Gary Ryan of _[NME](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NME "NME")_ said, "All in all, _The Lockdown Sessions_ all-bets-off stylistic game of spin-the-bottle feels attuned to 2021's post-genre Spotify world, as Elton continues to further his musical universe. The Rocketman remains in orbit."[\[26\]](#cite_note-nme-26) Kate Hutchinson of _[The Observer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Observer "The Observer")_ said, "It's all fun, though a little disjointed – and the less said about Elton's trap song, Always Love You, with Nicki Minaj and Young Thug, the better."[\[27\]](#cite_note-theobserver-27) Rich Wilhelm of _[PopMatters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PopMatters "PopMatters")_ said, "_The Lockdown Sessions_ is an engaging series of snapshots of time well-spent."[\[28\]](#cite_note-popmatters-28) Jon Dolan of _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ said, "Even if this project probably won't give us any fresh entrants into the large canon of classic Elton songs, _The Lockdown Sessions_ is still a glowing testament to his enduring pop gravitas."[\[29\]](#cite_note-rollingstone-29) Stephen Troussé of _[Uncut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uncut_\(magazine\) "Uncut (magazine)")_ called the album "a rum selection of Zoom collaborations with everyone from Dua Lipa to Lil Nas X, that old keenness is still there, though only on "It's a Sin," his Brits team-up with Olly Alexander."[\[30\]](#cite_note-uncut-30) Annie Zaleski of _[Variety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety_\(magazine\) "Variety (magazine)")_ said, "John's open-hearted vocals and sincerity make _The Lockdown Sessions_ a charming listen."[\[31\]](#cite_note-31)

## Commercial performance

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=The_Lockdown_Sessions_\(Elton_John_album\)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Commercial performance")\]

The album was released on 22 October 2021, and in the [OCC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Official_Charts_Company "Official Charts Company")'s UK midweek chart update on 25 October, the album was described as being in a "four way battle" with [Duran Duran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duran_Duran "Duran Duran")'s _[Future Past](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Future_Past_\(Duran_Duran_album\) "Future Past (Duran Duran album)")_, [Lana Del Rey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lana_Del_Rey "Lana Del Rey")'s _[Blue Banisters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_Banisters "Blue Banisters")_ and [Biffy Clyro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biffy_Clyro "Biffy Clyro")'s _[The Myth of the Happily Ever After](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Myth_of_the_Happily_Ever_After "The Myth of the Happily Ever After")_ for the number-one position.[\[32\]](#cite_note-32) It later became John's eighth number-one album in the UK on 29 October 2021, his first number-one album since 2012's _[Good Morning to the Night](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Good_Morning_to_the_Night "Good Morning to the Night")_.[\[33\]](#cite_note-33)

_The Lockdown Sessions_ achieved 31,000 chart sales in the UK, 84% of which were physical (CD and vinyl) sales in the first week. It was John's second number one in the UK in less than a month – "Cold Heart (Pnau remix)" with Dua Lipa reached number one on the UK Singles Chart earlier in the month.[\[34\]](#cite_note-34) In the United States, the album debuted at number ten on the [_Billboard_ 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200 "Billboard 200") with first-week sales of 29,000 album-equivalent units, 17,000 of that sum were pure album copies, it went straight to number four on the U.S. [Top Album Sales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Top_Album_Sales "Top Album Sales") chart.[\[35\]](#cite_note-35)[\[36\]](#cite_note-36)

text:
# Abracadabra (Lady Gaga song)

i/67th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "67th Annual Grammy Awards") on February 2.[\[a\]](#cite_note-11)

"Abracadabra" was released for [digital download](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_download "Music download") and [streaming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Streaming_media "Streaming media") platforms on February 3, 2025, through [Interscope Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interscope_Records "Interscope Records").[\[11\]](#cite_note-AppleM-12) It was subsequently serviced to Italian radio,[\[12\]](#cite_note-AirplayControl-13) followed by contemporary hit radio in the United States on February 11, 2025.[\[13\]](#cite_note-USRadio-14)

## Writing and recording

During an episode of the _[Song Exploder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Song_Exploder "Song Exploder")_ podcast, Gaga explained that she and her collaborators were initially working on a slower song that was ultimately scrapped from _Mayhem_.[\[14\]](#cite_note-15) When producer [Cirkut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cirkut "Cirkut") later played her an instrumental he had been developing, she was drawn to its intensity and decided to begin a new song, which became "Abracadabra".[\[15\]](#cite_note-SongExploder-16) The first line she wrote was "Like a poem said by a lady in red, you hear the last few words of your life", which she intended to evoke the preparation of a spell in a ritual.[\[15\]](#cite_note-SongExploder-16) This was followed by the creation of the chord progression, which Cirkut incorporated into the track to form the chorus. [Song engineer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audio_engineer "Audio engineer") Paul Lamalfa compiled a selection of words to shape the song's stuttering post-chorus, including "amor" and "morta", [Latin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin "Latin") for "love" and "death", respectively.[\[15\]](#cite_note-SongExploder-16)

In an interview with _[The Howard Stern Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Howard_Stern_Show "The Howard Stern Show")_, Gaga said the song came together quickly, with the track, verses, and chorus taking about 30 minutes to complete. She contrasted this with other songs from _Mayhem_, which sometimes took longer to finalize.[\[16\]](#cite_note-17) Producer [Andrew Watt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Watt "Andrew Watt") described the recording sessions as "spontaneous", explaining that she immediately responded to the instrumental by grabbing the microphone and beginning to freestyle.[\[17\]](#cite_note-Wattrs-18) He noted that once the initial idea emerged, she would move to the piano to shape the song's chord structure, after which the arrangement was further developed through layered synthesizers and iterative recording between the control room and live room.[\[17\]](#cite_note-Wattrs-18)

## Composition and production

![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cb/Gnome-mime-audio-openclipart.svg/60px-Gnome-mime-audio-openclipart.svg.png)

"Abracadabra" was written and produced by Gaga, Andrew Watt, and Cirkut. Additionally, [Siouxsie and the Banshees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siouxsie_and_the_Banshees "Siouxsie and the Banshees") members [Susan Janet Ballion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siouxsie_Sioux "Siouxsie Sioux"), [Peter Edward Clarke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Budgie_\(musician\) "Budgie (musician)"), [Steven Severin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Severin "Steven Severin"), and [John McGeoch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McGeoch "John McGeoch") received songwriting credits, as it incorporates elements from their 1981 single "[Spellbound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spellbound_\(Siouxsie_and_the_Banshees_song\) "Spellbound (Siouxsie and the Banshees song)")".[\[18\]](#cite_note-Puremédias_1-19) The track features lead vocals and keyboards by Gaga, with additional instrumentation by Watt and programming by Cirkut.[\[1\]](#cite_note-Liner-Notes-1) It was recorded at [Shangri-La](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shangri-La_\(recording_studio\) "Shangri-La (recording studio)") Studios in Malibu and later mixed and mastered by [Serban Ghenea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serban_Ghenea "Serban Ghenea") and [Randy Merrill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randy_Merrill "Randy Merrill"), respectively.[\[1\]](#cite_note-Liner-Notes-1)

## Writing and recording

During an episode of the _[Song Exploder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Song_Exploder "Song Exploder")_ podcast, Gaga explained that she and her collaborators were initially working on a slower song that was ultimately scrapped from _Mayhem_.[\[14\]](#cite_note-15) When producer [Cirkut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cirkut "Cirkut") later played her an instrumental he had been developing, she was drawn to its intensity and decided to begin a new song, which became "Abracadabra".[\[15\]](#cite_note-SongExploder-16) The first line she wrote was "Like a poem said by a lady in red, you hear the last few words of your life", which she intended to evoke the preparation of a spell in a ritual.[\[15\]](#cite_note-SongExploder-16) This was followed by the creation of the chord progression, which Cirkut incorporated into the track to form the chorus. [Song engineer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audio_engineer "Audio engineer") Paul Lamalfa compiled a selection of words to shape the song's stuttering post-chorus, including "amor" and "morta", [Latin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin "Latin") for "love" and "death", respectively.[\[15\]](#cite_note-SongExploder-16)

In an interview with _[The Howard Stern Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Howard_Stern_Show "The Howard Stern Show")_, Gaga said the song came together quickly, with the track, verses, and chorus taking about 30 minutes to complete. She contrasted this with other songs from _Mayhem_, which sometimes took longer to finalize.[\[16\]](#cite_note-17) Producer [Andrew Watt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Watt "Andrew Watt") described the recording sessions as "spontaneous", explaining that she immediately responded to the instrumental by grabbing the microphone and beginning to freestyle.[\[17\]](#cite_note-Wattrs-18) He noted that once the initial idea emerged, she would move to the piano to shape the song's chord structure, after which the arrangement was further developed through layered synthesizers and iterative recording between the control room and live room.[\[17\]](#cite_note-Wattrs-18)

te-Switzerland-110)[\[111\]](#cite_note-Uruguay-111) The song received a gold [certifications](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_recording_certification "Music recording certification") from [IFPI Greece](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IFPI_Greece "IFPI Greece") in Greece and [IFPI Switzerland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Federation_of_the_Phonographic_Industry "International Federation of the Phonographic Industry") in Switzerland.[\[112\]](#cite_note-Greece_Cert-112)[\[113\]](#cite_note-Switzerland_Cert-113) It was certified double platinum in Denmark,[\[114\]](#cite_note-Denmark_Cert-114) Mexico[\[115\]](#cite_note-Mexico_Cert-115) and Norway[\[116\]](#cite_note-Norway_Cert-116) as well as triple platinum in Austria,[\[117\]](#cite_note-Austria_Cert-117) Italy,[\[118\]](#cite_note-Italy_Cert-118) Portugal,[\[119\]](#cite_note-Portugal_Cert-119) and Sweden,[\[120\]](#cite_note-Sweden_Cert-120) and six-times Platinum in Spain.[\[121\]](#cite_note-Spain_Cert-121) The song further garnered a diamond certification from the [Syndicat National de l'Édition Phonographique](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syndicat_National_de_l'Édition_Phonographique "Syndicat National de l'Édition Phonographique") (SNEP) in France and the [Polish Society of the Phonographic Industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polish_Society_of_the_Phonographic_Industry "Polish Society of the Phonographic Industry") (ZPAV) in Poland.[\[122\]](#cite_note-France_Cert-122)[\[123\]](#cite_note-Poland_Cert-123)

Scene from the [music video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_video "Music video") of "Cold Heart (Pnau remix)", showcasing Elton John and Dua Lipa as [animated characters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Character_animation "Character animation") celebrating on one side of the [Milky Way](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milky_Way "Milky Way")[\[124\]](#cite_note-Video-124)[\[125\]](#cite_note-CRM-125)

To accompany the release, a [music video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_video "Music video") for "Cold Heart (Pnau remix)" premiered to John's official [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube") channel on 13 August 2021.[\[124\]](#cite_note-Video-124) Created in the isolation of the pandemic, Raman Djafari of [Blink Ink](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blink_\(company\)#Blinkink "Blink (company)") directed the animated and imaginative video with the aspiration of crafting a galaxy "full of celebration, dance and joy".[\[126\]](#cite_note-Brewer-126)[\[125\]](#cite_note-CRM-125) Gareth Owen and Josef Byrne produced the video with the characters of John and Lipa being designed by Seo Young.[\[127\]](#cite_note-Milligan-127) The video traces the adventure of John and Lipa, portrayed as animated characters, together with four [claymation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claymation "Claymation")\-described 3D characters that dance to disco music, as they explore colorful and nature-filled galaxies and [psychedelic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychedelic_art "Psychedelic art") landscapes.[\[126\]](#cite_note-Brewer-126)[\[125\]](#cite_note-CRM-125) In a sequence, the use of hand-drawn 2D elements enhances the visual frames, imparting an ethereal atmosphere to the animation.[\[124\]](#cite_note-Video-124) One of the dancers draws a shooting star in the sky, while flying fish appear to radiate from the movements of their dancing shoes.[\[126\]](#cite_note-Brewer-126) At the same time, towering flowers with eyes emerge and envelop the dancers, imbuing them with a sense of nature.[\[124\]](#cite_note-Video-124) There is also a psychedelic countryside sequence featuring flowers with puckered petals that sway in time with the music, and clouds fashioned into the shapes of [unicorns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unicorn "Unicorn") and castles.[\[126\]](#cite_note-Brewer-126) The animated characters bring their journey to a close by joining John and Lipa in a dance celebration at a garden party located on one side of the [Milky Way](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milky_Way "Milky Way").[\[124\]](#cite_note-Video-124)[\[125\]](#cite_note-CRM-125) John Russell from _[Grazia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grazia "Grazia")_ expressed his admiration for the video, while characterising it as "gorgeous" and highlighting its animation theme.[\[128\]](#cite_note-128) Robledo for _Gay Times_ referred to the video as "stunning" and deemed it to be "a fun and mind-blowing experience".[\[20\]](#cite_note-Robledo-20) Paulina Vales of _The Honey Pop_ declared the video as the year's "most iconic animated video" and commended its aesthetics and fashion, writing that "\[John and Lipa brought\] us joy we were missing in our life".[\[129\]](#cite_note-129)

While being streamed by American streaming platform [Disney+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney+ "Disney+"), John and Lipa performed "Cold Heart (Pnau remix)" live at [Dodger Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dodger_Stadium "Dodger Stadium") in [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles") as part of the former's Farewell Yellow Brick Road world tour on 20 November 2022.[\[130\]](#cite_note-130) Three remixes of the song, including a rendition by German disc jockey [Claptone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claptone "Claptone") and American disc jockey [the Blessed Madonna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Blessed_Madonna "The Blessed Madonna"), accompanied the single's release between September and October 2021.[\[131\]](#cite_note-CH_CR-131)[\[132\]](#cite_note-CH_PS1-132)[\[133\]](#cite_note-CH_TBMR-133) The rendition by the Blessed Madonna marked the second time that she had remixed a song from Lipa, following [the remix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Levitating_\(The_Blessed_Madonna_remix\) "Levitating (The Blessed Madonna remix)") of "[Levitating](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Levitating_\(song\) "Levitating (song)")" (2020).[\[134\]](#cite_note-Reis2-134) Samantha Reis from _We Rave You_ gave a favorable assessment of the remix, stating that it took the already "club-ready beat" and elevated its "clubby vibe" to the maximum.[\[134\]](#cite_note-Reis2-134) Ariel King for [Dancing Astronaut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dancing_Astronaut "Dancing Astronaut") also positively commented that the remix "fits neatly into a sparkling club atmosphere while maintaining Lipa's disco aesthetic".[\[135\]](#cite_note-135) The remix was accompanied by a visualiser video as a remix of the official music video, displaying animated eyes and fantastical creatures.[\[136\]](#cite_note-136)[\[137\]](#cite_note-137)

# Cold Heart (Pnau remix)

te-Switzerland-110)[\[111\]](#cite_note-Uruguay-111) The song received a gold [certifications](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_recording_certification "Music recording certification") from [IFPI Greece](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IFPI_Greece "IFPI Greece") in Greece and [IFPI Switzerland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Federation_of_the_Phonographic_Industry "International Federation of the Phonographic Industry") in Switzerland.[\[112\]](#cite_note-Greece_Cert-112)[\[113\]](#cite_note-Switzerland_Cert-113) It was certified double platinum in Denmark,[\[114\]](#cite_note-Denmark_Cert-114) Mexico[\[115\]](#cite_note-Mexico_Cert-115) and Norway[\[116\]](#cite_note-Norway_Cert-116) as well as triple platinum in Austria,[\[117\]](#cite_note-Austria_Cert-117) Italy,[\[118\]](#cite_note-Italy_Cert-118) Portugal,[\[119\]](#cite_note-Portugal_Cert-119) and Sweden,[\[120\]](#cite_note-Sweden_Cert-120) and six-times Platinum in Spain.[\[121\]](#cite_note-Spain_Cert-121) The song further garnered a diamond certification from the [Syndicat National de l'Édition Phonographique](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syndicat_National_de_l'Édition_Phonographique "Syndicat National de l'Édition Phonographique") (SNEP) in France and the [Polish Society of the Phonographic Industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polish_Society_of_the_Phonographic_Industry "Polish Society of the Phonographic Industry") (ZPAV) in Poland.[\[122\]](#cite_note-France_Cert-122)[\[123\]](#cite_note-Poland_Cert-123)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/d/d7/Elton_John_%26_Dua_Lipa_-_Cold_Heart_%28Pnau_remix%29_%28Screenshot%29.png/330px-Elton_John_%26_Dua_Lipa_-_Cold_Heart_%28Pnau_remix%29_%28Screenshot%29.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Elton_John_&_Dua_Lipa_-_Cold_Heart_\(Pnau_remix\)_\(Screenshot\).png)

Scene from the [music video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_video "Music video") of "Cold Heart (Pnau remix)", showcasing Elton John and Dua Lipa as [animated characters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Character_animation "Character animation") celebrating on one side of the [Milky Way](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milky_Way "Milky Way")[\[124\]](#cite_note-Video-124)[\[125\]](#cite_note-CRM-125)

To accompany the release, a [music video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_video "Music video") for "Cold Heart (Pnau remix)" premiered to John's official [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube") channel on 13 August 2021.[\[124\]](#cite_note-Video-124) Created in the isolation of the pandemic, Raman Djafari of [Blink Ink](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blink_\(company\)#Blinkink "Blink (company)") directed the animated and imaginative video with the aspiration of crafting a galaxy "full of celebration, dance and joy".[\[126\]](#cite_note-Brewer-126)[\[125\]](#cite_note-CRM-125) Gareth Owen and Josef Byrne produced the video with the characters of John and Lipa being designed by Seo Young.[\[127\]](#cite_note-Milligan-127) The video traces the adventure of John and Lipa, portrayed as animated characters, together with four [claymation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claymation "Claymation")\-described 3D characters that dance to disco music, as they explore colorful and nature-filled galaxies and [psychedelic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychedelic_art "Psychedelic art") landscapes.[\[126\]](#cite_note-Brewer-126)[\[125\]](#cite_note-CRM-125) In a sequence, the use of hand-drawn 2D elements enhances the visual frames, imparting an ethereal atmosphere to the animation.[\[124\]](#cite_note-Video-124) One of the dancers draws a shooting star in the sky, while flying fish appear to radiate from the movements of their dancing shoes.[\[126\]](#cite_note-Brewer-126) At the same time, towering flowers with eyes emerge and envelop the dancers, imbuing them with a sense of nature.[\[124\]](#cite_note-Video-124) There is also a psychedelic countryside sequence featuring flowers with puckered petals that sway in time with the music, and clouds fashioned into the shapes of [unicorns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unicorn "Unicorn") and castles.[\[126\]](#cite_note-Brewer-126) The animated characters bring their journey to a close by joining John and Lipa in a dance celebration at a garden party located on one side of the [Milky Way](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milky_Way "Milky Way").[\[124\]](#cite_note-Video-124)[\[125\]](#cite_note-CRM-125) John Russell from _[Grazia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grazia "Grazia")_ expressed his admiration for the video, while characterising it as "gorgeous" and highlighting its animation theme.[\[128\]](#cite_note-128) Robledo for _Gay Times_ referred to the video as "stunning" and deemed it to be "a fun and mind-blowing experience".[\[20\]](#cite_note-Robledo-20) Paulina Vales of _The Honey Pop_ declared the video as the year's "most iconic animated video" and commended its aesthetics and fashion, writing that "\[John and Lipa brought\] us joy we were missing in our life".[\[129\]](#cite_note-129)

While being streamed by American streaming platform [Disney+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney+ "Disney+"), John and Lipa performed "Cold Heart (Pnau remix)" live at [Dodger Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dodger_Stadium "Dodger Stadium") in [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles") as part of the former's Farewell Yellow Brick Road world tour on 20 November 2022.[\[130\]](#cite_note-130) Three remixes of the song, including a rendition by German disc jockey [Claptone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claptone "Claptone") and American disc jockey [the Blessed Madonna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Blessed_Madonna "The Blessed Madonna"), accompanied the single's release between September and October 2021.[\[131\]](#cite_note-CH_CR-131)[\[132\]](#cite_note-CH_PS1-132)[\[133\]](#cite_note-CH_TBMR-133) The rendition by the Blessed Madonna marked the second time that she had remixed a song from Lipa, following [the remix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Levitating_\(The_Blessed_Madonna_remix\) "Levitating (The Blessed Madonna remix)") of "[Levitating](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Levitating_\(song\) "Levitating (song)")" (2020).[\[134\]](#cite_note-Reis2-134) Samantha Reis from _We Rave You_ gave a favorable assessment of the remix, stating that it took the already "club-ready beat" and elevated its "clubby vibe" to the maximum.[\[134\]](#cite_note-Reis2-134) Ariel King for [Dancing Astronaut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dancing_Astronaut "Dancing Astronaut") also positively commented that the remix "fits neatly into a sparkling club atmosphere while maintaining Lipa's disco aesthetic".[\[135\]](#cite_note-135) The remix was accompanied by a visualiser video as a remix of the official music video, displaying animated eyes and fantastical creatures.[\[136\]](#cite_note-136)[\[137\]](#cite_note-137)

text:
# Abracadabra (Lady Gaga song)

 "abracadabra" is incorporated into the song's post-chorus, albeit with "broken syntax".[\[27\]](#cite_note-PinkAbracadabra-28) In the song's refrain, a "lady in red" is mentioned, which Gaga described as representing every individual's "internal monologue" asking if they are good enough.[\[35\]](#cite_note-Elle_1-36) She further explained that the song explores resilience and perseverance, using the dance floor as a metaphor for confronting self-doubt and pushing oneself to grow rather than merely survive.[\[35\]](#cite_note-Elle_1-36) Writing for _[InStyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/InStyle "InStyle")_, Jonathan Borge wrote that the song "explores the duality of an artist battling the desire to constantly evolve sonically, aesthetically, and as a human, while facing extraordinary creative pressure".[\[36\]](#cite_note-InStyle_1-37) Gina Wurtz of _[Screen Rant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen_Rant "Screen Rant")_ described the song's message as "deeper than it appears on the surface", interpreting its lyrics as an encouragement to ignore negative voices and stay focused on one's own path.[\[37\]](#cite_note-ScreenRant-38) _[Elite Daily](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elite_Daily "Elite Daily")_ theorized that the use of the word "amor" could also serve as a hidden nod to "Bad Romance", as its reverse spelling ("roma") is a recurring word in that chorus.[\[38\]](#cite_note-39) Many journalists have compared the song's dark and theatrical style to Gaga's earlier songs, including those from _[The Fame Monster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fame_Monster "The Fame Monster")_ (2009) and _[Chromatica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromatica "Chromatica")_ (2020).[\[19\]](#cite_note-USA_Today_1-20)[\[24\]](#cite_note-HuffPost_UK-25)[\[39\]](#cite_note-DIY_1-40)

"Abracadabra" was frequently ranked as one of the best songs of 2025 and was included in various year-end lists from music critics. _Rolling Stone_'s Kory Grow ranked it at number one, highlighting its dynamic synth work, sweeping hook, and the way it channels her early pop sensibilities.[\[46\]](#cite_note-RS2025-48) Wesley Stenzel of _Entertainment Weekly_ also placed it at number one, praising its blend of gothic theatricality, powerful vocals, and club-oriented production.[\[58\]](#cite_note-entweekly-61) _Billboard_'s Joe Lynch placed the track at number two, describing it as a "sleazy, slinky club banger" that showcases her vocal maturity.[\[42\]](#cite_note-Billboard2025-43) The song placed at number four on _[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Guardian "The Guardian")_'s list, where Ben Beaumont-Thomas highlighted its dual house beats and "double the fun" flair,[\[25\]](#cite_note-TheGuardian-26) and also ranked fourth on _USA Today_'s year-end list, with Melissa Ruggieri highlighting i

# Cold Heart (PNAU Remix) by Elton John (featuring Dua Lipa) - Songfacts

![Play Video](https://img.youtube.com/vi/qod03PVTLqk/hqdefault.jpg)

#### Songfacts®:

*   This club-ready single blends together four of Elton John's much-loved tracks for a song about a relationship that's gone icy. It starts with John performing lyrics from his 1989 single "[Sacrifice](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/elton-john/sacrifice)," then Dua Lipa comes in for the chorus borrowed from Elton's 1972 hit "[Rocket Man](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/elton-john/rocket-man)." The song also features elements from "Kiss The Bride" (originally from the 1983 album **Too Low For Zero**), and "Where's the Shoorah?" (from the 1976 double album **Blue Moves**).
    
*   Dua Lipa planted the seed of the collaboration when she invited Elton John for an Instagram live discussion of his experiences with Studio 54 ahead of her remix album **Club Future Nostalgia**. A subsequent friendship blossomed, which saw John appear as a guest on Lipa's Studio 2054 live stream. The two then sang together at Elton's 2021 Oscars party, performing "[Bennie And The Jets](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/elton-john/bennie-and-the-jets)" and "[Love Again](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/dua-lipa/love-again)."
    
*   The Australian dance music trio PNAU cobbled together the production. PNAU previously released an album of John remixes titled **Good Morning To The Night** in 2012. That record shared a similar approach to this dance blender, taking samples from John's catalog of recordings and mixing them together to create completely new anthems.
    
*   The Hamburg-based animator and director Raman Djafari created the video, which sees animated versions of the two singers stepping into a vibrant and euphoric world before separating as their planets drift apart.
    
*   This became Elton John's 68th career entry on the Hot 100 when it debuted at #81 on the chart dated August 28. The English icon's previous visit to the chart was 21 years previously when "Someday Out of the Blue" ranked at #99 on the chart dated July 29, 2000, after reaching #49.
    
*   When "Cold Heart" entered the UK Top 10 in September 2021, Elton John became the first artist to rack up a Top 10 song in the UK in six different decades. He overtook Cher, Cliff Richard, Elvis Presley, Michael Jackson and David Bowie, who each scored at least one Top 10 single in five different decades.
    
*   The song climbed to #1 on the UK singles chart after three consecutive weeks #2. It marked Elton John's eighth visit to the UK summit and first for 16 years, since his feature on 2Pac's posthumous 2005 single "[Ghetto Gospel](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/2pac/ghetto-gospel)."
    
    Dua Lipa achieved her third UK #1 with this song. Her previous two chart-toppers were her 2017 solo single "[New Rules](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/dua-lipa/new-rules)" and her 2018 collaboration with Calvin Harris, "[One Kiss](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/calvin-harris/one-kiss)."
    
*   When the song jumped from #46 to #32 on the Hot 100, it gave Elton his first Top 40 hit since his duet with LeAnn Rimes in 1999, "Written In The Stars." It also broke the record for longest span between first and last Top 40 hit. Elton's first Top 40 was "[Your Song](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/elton-john/your-song)," which he released in 1970.
    
    Michael Jackson previously had the record with his 1971 hit "[Ben](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/michael-jackson/ben)" to his posthumous feature on Drake's 2018 song "[Don't Matter to Me](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/drake/dont-matter-to-me)."
    
*   **The Lockdown Sessions** became Elton's eighth UK #1 album and his first since 2012's **Good Morning To The Night**.
    
*   When this climbed to #1 in Australia, Elton, at 74 years, seven months and 14 days, became the oldest artist to top the ARIA Singles Chart. He overtook Paul McCartney, who reached the summit with "[FourFiveSeconds](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/rihanna/fourfiveseconds)," alongside Rihanna and Kanye West, when he was 72.
    
*   "Cold Heart" is just one taster from eight months of work for PNAU remixing Elton John tracks. "We ended up making 12 to 14 songs. It's full of dance bangers, it's not as broad as (Elton John's) collaborations album," PNAU's Nick Littlemore told [Billboard](https://www.billboard.com/music/music-news/pnau-nick-littlemore-elton-john-empire-of-the-sun-interview-1235004590/).
    
*   The song spent 10 weeks at #1 on the Australian singles chart. An impressive achievement, but well short of the record held by Tones and I's "[Dance Monkey](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/magic/dance-monkey)," which stayed at the summit for 24 weeks.
    
*   "Cold Heart" re-entered the UK Singles Chart at #30 after Elton John performed it at Glastonbury 2023. Elton's Sunday Pyramid Stage headline slot was promoted as his potentially last-ever UK live show.
    
    Dua Lipa failed to show up on stage to perform her duet vocals with Elton. "The person I did the song with isn't here, so I'm going to ask you to sing her part – and sing it loudly," said the showbiz veteran when introducing "Cold Heart."

He overtook Paul McCartney, who reached the summit with "[FourFiveSeconds](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/rihanna/fourfiveseconds)," alongside Rihanna and Kanye West, when he was 72.
    
*   "Cold Heart" is just one taster from eight months of work for PNAU remixing Elton John tracks. "We ended up making 12 to 14 songs. It's full of dance bangers, it's not as broad as (Elton John's) collaborations album," PNAU's Nick Littlemore told [Billboard](https://www.billboard.com/music/music-news/pnau-nick-littlemore-elton-john-empire-of-the-sun-interview-1235004590/).
    
*   The song spent 10 weeks at #1 on the Australian singles chart. An impressive achievement, but well short of the record held by Tones and I's "[Dance Monkey](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/magic/dance-monkey)," which stayed at the summit for 24 weeks.
    
*   "Cold Heart" re-entered the UK Singles Chart at #30 after Elton John performed it at Glastonbury 2023. Elton's Sunday Pyramid Stage headline slot was promoted as his potentially last-ever UK live show.
    
    Dua Lipa failed to show up on stage to perform her duet vocals with Elton. "The person I did the song with isn't here, so I'm going to ask you to sing her part – and sing it loudly," said the showbiz veteran when introducing "Cold Heart."

# Pnau on how they produced Elton John and Dua Lipa’s Cold Heart: “We had the tapes from Elton’s whole career, so there was a lot to choose from”

 ![Dua Lipa and Elton John](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/aZJYJBy7L9xtu7aDLtZ7Za.jpg)

(Image credit: David M. Benett/Getty Images for the Elton John AIDS Foundation)

**Elton John’s Glastonbury performance is set to be one of the highlights of this weekend’s festival, and emotions are bound to run high. This will be both his first appearance at Worthy Farm and the last UK date on his swansong Farewell Yellow Brick Road tour, making it potentially his last show on British shores (though we’d bet against that being the case).**

The man born Reg Dwight has an almost unrivalled back catalogue of songs to draw on for his Glastonbury set, but younger festival goers may actually know Elton best for Cold Heart, the Pnau-remixed track that he released in 2021. A duet with Dua Lipa - who’s tipped to make a guest appearance at Glastonbury - this hit number 1 in the UK and was a global hit.

Pnau are an Australian dance music trio comprising Nick Littlemore, Peter Mayes and Sam Littlemore, and earlier this year, Nick and Peter spoke to [Music Week](https://www.musicweek.com/interviews/read/hitmakers-pnau-s-nick-littlemore-peter-mayes-on-the-making-of-elton-john-dua-lipa-s-cold-heart/087408) (Paywall) about how Cold Heart came about.

The origins of the song can be traced back more than a decade, as Pnau first collaborated with Elton on a whole album of remixes of his songs, Good Morning To The Night, which was released in 2012.

> Cold Heart started with Elton asking us to take on his catalogue again. And this time, he wanted a hit single.

“Cold Heart started with Elton asking us to take on his catalogue again,” says Nick Littlemore. “And this time, he wanted a hit single. He didn’t want us to just make something artful, it was more about making something that was going to ignite the hearts, ears and minds of the global music community.”

This was in May 2020, right at the start of the Covid pandemic, meaning that getting everyone in a room together was impossible.

“We were in separate studios in Downtown LA and it was complete lockdown,” recalls Peter Mayes. “We didn’t know anything about Covid and everyone was bleaching their groceries, it was crazy times. No one was hanging out with anyone, but the music world was very much moving towards remote working anyway.”

Want all the hottest music and gear news, reviews, deals, features and more, direct to your inbox? Sign up here.

Cold Heart is actually an amalgamation of four Elton songs: Sacrifice, Rocket Man, Kiss The Bride and Where’s The Shoorah? However, it took a while for these tracks to be decided on.

“We had the tapes from Elton’s whole career, so there was a lot to choose from,” says Peter Mayes. “We’d done a lot of the more obscure ’70s stuff on the previous album, but we wanted to do something bigger, focus more on vocals and have a radio moment. We hadn’t delved into Elton’s ’80s and ’90s catalogue much, but Nick was messing around with Sacrifice and sent it to me.

“I was like, ‘Okay, cool. Sacrifice is fair game then,’ so the verse is from Sacrifice and then the chorus is from Rocket Man. We didn’t want to use the bit where it says ‘Rocket man’ though, because then it would have become Rocket Man. We found that the pre-chorus from Kiss The Bride worked as a post-chorus in Cold Heart, and then there was the Where’s The Shoorah? section which was for the outro.”

In hindsight, the Rocket Man chorus seems like a natural fit, but it wasn’t always a shoo-in for inclusion.

“I had five or six other options for the chorus apart from Rocket Man,” Mayes confirms. “I would drive around with a list of songs and listen to the verse, and there’d be a big gap where the chorus was, so I’d just try and sing any other Elton song over it and see if it would work. Elton has done 50 albums or something, so there were a lot of options - a lot of hits, great melodies and lyrics.”

What other choruses could have made the cut, then?

“I probably have a list of notes somewhere on my phone of songs I tried, but I don’t remember which others were considered,” says Mayes. “Probably Tiny Dancer, but it would have had to have been close in key. It was long before the Dua Lipa vocal at this stage, it was all Elton and I had to pick things that were very close in key and tempo. In the case of Rocket Man, I slowed it down a bit to make it work.”

Today’s timestretching and pitchshifting features gave Pnau a certain amount of flexibility, then, but that didn’t mean that every Elton song was fair game. “There were good ideas we could have used but we’d have been moving it too far away from the original recording,” explains Nick Littlemore.

“That’s exactly right,” adds Peter Mayes. “Once you’ve picked the key and tempo, you don’t actually have that many options. You’d think, ‘Can I move this up or down three semitones?’ But Elton would sound weird if you did that, because you can’t really move a vocal that much. You can with other instruments, but with vocals it just sounds silly and I don’t think Elton would have been into a chipmunk version of himself!”

Dua Lipa’s vocal parts, of course, were newly recorded, but she wasn’t involved until pretty late in the day.

“Dua Lipa came in right at the end,” says Peter Mayes. “I prepared it for the mix and her people put the vocals on it. We were basically like, ‘Great, Dua Lipa’s on the record, she can do whatever she wants!’”

Nick Littlemore says that he immediately knew Cold Heart was a hit - “Our hearts were bursting out of our chests when we heard it” - and it could easily have led to another whole album of Pnau/Elton John collaborations.

“Elton’s people were asking for more songs like Cold Heart the whole time,” reveals Peter Mayes. “It was the first one we delivered to him with another song and I think the plan was to do an album, but he decided to make an album of collaborations because he’d worked with so many people during the pandemic. So it made sense that the track became the lead single.”

As well as giving Elton John yet another career resurgence, Cold Heart has taken Pnau to another level, too. “It’s opened so many doors for us,” says Nick Littlemore. “We ended up inking a deal with Sony Music out of Germany and we’re now working with some of the biggest pop stars in the world. I don’t know how many we can mention, but if we opened a bag right now, a lot of names would drop out!”

I’m the Deputy Editor of MusicRadar, having worked on the site since its launch in 2007. I previously spent eight years working on our sister magazine, Computer Music. I’ve been playing the piano, gigging in bands and failing to finish tracks at home for more than 30 years, 24 of which I’ve also spent writing about music and the ever-changing technology used to make it.

On its release day, "Abracadabra" recorded 4.92 million streams on [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify "Spotify"), marking Gaga's biggest debut on the platform with a solo song.[\[65\]](#cite_note-Jenesaispop_2-68) Internationally, the song debuted at number ten on the [_Billboard_ Global 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Global_200 "Billboard Global 200") with 47.7 million streams, becoming the second top-ten entry from _Mayhem_ and of Gaga's career, after "[Die with a Smile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Die_with_a_Smile "Die with a Smile")".[\[66\]](#cite_note-Billboard_Global_200_1-69) In its second week, the song rose to a new peak of number five on the _Billboard_ Global 200 with 78.4 million streams.[\[67\]](#cite_note-70)

"**Die with a Smile**" is a song by American singer-songwriters [Lady Gaga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lady_Gaga "Lady Gaga") and [Bruno Mars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruno_Mars "Bruno Mars"). It was released as a standalone single on August 16, 2024, through [Interscope Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interscope_Records "Interscope Records"), and was included as the closing track of Gaga's studio album _[Mayhem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayhem_\(Lady_Gaga_album\) "Mayhem (Lady Gaga album)")_ (2025). Mars developed the track with [Dernst "D'Mile" Emile II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Mile "D'Mile") and [James Fauntleroy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Fauntleroy "James Fauntleroy") in 2021; three years later, he presented it to Gaga, and the four completed it the same day. The final version was written by Gaga, Mars, D-Mile, [Andrew Watt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Watt "Andrew Watt"), and Fauntleroy, and it was produced by the first four.

The song is a [sentimental ballad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sentimental_ballad "Sentimental ballad") that incorporates [pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_music "Pop music"), [pop-soul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop-soul "Pop-soul"), and [soft rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soft_rock "Soft rock"), with influences from [country music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_music "Country music"). Critics compared its style to the sounds of 1970s ballads, Gaga's album _[Joanne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joanne_\(album\) "Joanne (album)")_ (2016) and single "[Shallow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shallow_\(Lady_Gaga_and_Bradley_Cooper_song\) "Shallow (Lady Gaga and Bradley Cooper song)")" (2018), and Mars's [Silk Sonic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silk_Sonic "Silk Sonic") project. Lyrically, it expresses a powerful longing to be with a loved one, highlighting love's urgency amid uncertainty. The song received critical acclaim for the vocals, the instrumentation, and the lyrics' emotional weight.

"Die with a Smile" enjoyed widespread commercial success. On [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify "Spotify"), it became the [longest-reigning daily number-one song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Spotify_streaming_records#Longest-running_number-one_songs_by_days "List of Spotify streaming records"), the fastest track to surpass three billion streams, and the most-streamed song of 2025. The track spent 18 weeks atop the [_Billboard_ Global 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Global_200 "Billboard Global 200") and topped the charts in more than 30 countries, including the United States, Canada, New Zealand, and the Netherlands. It was [certified](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_recording_certification "Music recording certification") multi-diamond in Brazil by [Pro-Música Brasil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pro-Música_Brasil "Pro-Música Brasil") (PMB) and diamond in France by the [National Syndicate of Phonographic Publishing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Syndicate_of_Phonographic_Publishing "National Syndicate of Phonographic Publishing") (SNEP) and in Poland by the [Polish Society of the Phonographic Industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polish_Society_of_the_Phonographic_Industry "Polish Society of the Phonographic Industry") (ZPAV).

Mars and Daniel Ramos directed the music video, which was released simultaneously with the song. The video features Gaga playing piano and Mars playing guitar as they sing together in a studio inspired by 1970s television.

Wattage

One of music’s most in-demand producers spills on Gaga’s “The Dead Dance,” Carlile’s new album, and more

Producer/songwriter [Andrew Watt](https://www.rollingstone.com/t/andrew-watt/)‘s started off his wild year with [Lady Gaga](https://www.rollingstone.com/t/lady-gaga/)‘s smash _Mayhem_, co-producing and co-writing with Gaga, Cirkut, and others, and earning an executive producer credit alongside Gaga and Michael Polansky.  A month later came [Brandi Carlile](https://www.rollingstone.com/t/brandi-carlile/) and Elton John’s first album together, _Who Believes in Angels?,_ produced and co-written by Watt. Since then, he’s worked on [Katseye](https://www.rollingstone.com/t/katseye/)‘s single “Gabriela,” played at his friend Ozzy Osbourne’s final concert, and co-produced Carlile’s new solo album, _Returning to Myself_ (due Oct. 24) — and those are just the projects he can talk about.

Earlier this month, three different songs Watt worked on dropped in the same week —  Lady Gaga’s _Wednesday_ track _“_The Dead Dance” (co-produced and co-written with Gaga and Cirkut), Ed Sheeran’s “Camera,” and Carlile’s single “Returning to Myself.” (For even more from Watt, check out his episode of our Rolling Stone Music Now podcast on [Apple Podcasts](https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/rolling-stone-music-now/id1078431985) or [Spotify](https://open.spotify.com/show/0jCfnXfdYhwIM2I4x7SxZx), or just press play below.)

**Are you busier than you’ve ever been right now?**  
It’s been pretty much the same for a few years. Every day feels like Game Seven of the World Series. Wake up, “What are we doing today? Oh fuck. It’s time to bring it.” It’s not, “Oh, today’s just gonna be a relaxing day.” Every day there’s something really important to me that I’m working on. What more could you ask for out of life, right?

**Gaga’s “The Dead Dance” for _Wednesday_ is such a fun surprise, with a great disco-influenced feel.  
**She is unbelievable. Every one of these songs that we ever made together, the concepts are so effortlessly _her_. Lady Gaga, “The Dead Dance.” It’s just such a _her_ concept. Because of the title and the way that she was singing, the production morphed and shifted a lot. We worked very hard on that production to make it sound original and also feel like something that you could really dance to. 

What I really love about that song is the live instrumentation mixed with the track instrumentation. There’s some really good bass in there and cool guitar inversions and stuff and great synths and the way everything works together. I remember when we were making that bridge, that’s where it got _really_ funky. “Do the dead dance” — that was invented from the bridge music. That was a big telltale for the song. And then everything got morphed around that.

## Editor’s picks

**One really different thing you did recently was the Katseye song “Gabriela.” How did that come about?**  
Yeah. I’ve had some great success working with the guys, \[Hybe founder\] Bang \[Si-Hyuk\] and Jung Kook and those songs that we did \[in 2023\]. When he brought Katseye to me and was like, “This is my new thing,” we just worked to find the right song. To make a big song, especially in pop music, it takes an army, like literally an army, everything from the group to the managers to the label. Everything has to be firing on all cylinders. It went through Interscope — I absolutely love that team there, and John Janick, and they’re amazing at what they do. 

Katseye are like the new Spice Girls.I really enjoyed working with the different vocalists. Finding which singer should sing what and when it should come in — the puzzle of that was fun. It was like when I was young, I loved puzzles. 

**Katseye seem like potential superstars in the making.**  
I mean, they’re not in the making, they’re superstars! Absolutely. I’d love to do more with them. I think they’re just great.

**You did a lot of work with Aaron Dessner on Brandi Carlile’s new album; how did that cross-collaboration work?  
**Brandi was in an unbelievable period where she did this amazing collaboration with Joni \[Mitchell\]. Getting Joni [onstage again](https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/joni-mitchell-surprise-performance-brandi-carlile-hollywood-bowl-show-1234854721/) and taking that on her back? Brandi is one of the strongest-willed people that I’ve ever met in my life. She did that and then went straight from that into this Elton collaboration. After that, she was just feeling like, “What am I gonna do next? It’s time to turn inward.”  So she was searching, working in a way that she hasn’t worked before. David Bowie always said, “Swim into the deep end where your feet can’t touch the ground, and then that’s when you’ll really start making something.”  I made a really great friend out of Aaron, which is so cool. We love each other and we had so much fun. He worked on some of the things that I had started with Brandi and I worked on some of the things that he started with Brandi and it just became this kind of really open, great thing. 

## Related Content

**Where did your sensibilities meet and where, if at all, do they diverge?  
**Aaron is a master in subtlety, where you’re listening, and it’s very song-focused, and some beautiful sound — maybe some muted thing — goes by, and you can’t even tell what it really is. It just lifts your emotion. My music is not always very subtle. It’s kind of putting those two things together and getting them to work — maybe a song starting really subtle and then maybe building to something larger at the end. We were like checks and balances for each other. But we’re also, at our core,  both guitar players. So we just had so much fun playing guitar together. We would plug in together at the same time and play live. And the Brandi Carlile band is a live band. So it was important for the songs to still be recorded like a live band. 

**The title track is a beautiful, low-key song.**  
Yeah. We were messing around a lot with open tunings. Brandi Carlile played the album _Blue_ live at Carnegie. The confidence you have to do that!  She really got inside those songs. She understands the chords and how they change and how they move. So once that happens, you get a new bag of tricks. Her guitar player, Tim \[Hanseroth\], had his guitar in this really cool Joni tuning and she just picked up the guitar and that’s when “Returning to Myself” came out. That was the last song that got written. And it felt, as often, your last song that you make should be the first song. The song’s called “Returning to Myself.” So what do you hear? You hear her alone. And as the song grows, you start to hear these textures that maybe you haven’t heard on a Brandi song before, and they’re more esoteric and dreamlike. We talked a lot about _Wrecking Ball_, which Daniel Lanois produced for Emmylou Harris. You let Emmylou be exactly what Emmylou is, but all the sounds around her and the production is something that she hadn’t done before. It became a guiding light for us.

**You also have a new song, “Camera,” with Ed Sheeran.  
**The day we wrote “Camera,” we wrote three songs. Three full, finished songs. That was just one of them. One of them came out already, it was called “2step” \[released in 2021\].  
**  
Oh, so these sessions were a while ago. People have talked to me about the extraordinary speed that Ed writes songs.  
**The only way I can describe Ed is like Michael Jordan. It’s athletic, the way in which he writes songs and the way he’s working himself and the level in which he comes in. And it’s that Game Seven thing that I was talking to you about before. It’s like he steps in and he’s there to do it and he moves so quickly and you just gotta be there to follow it and be there for him. You’ve never seen anyone record harmonies the way he does. It’s amazing. They’re pitch-perfect, one after another. 

**Keith Richards’ son, Marlon Richards, let slip that the Rolling Stones are recording an album in London. And you happened to mention you were just recording something in London — and you worked with the Stones on their [last album](https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-album-reviews/rolling-stones-hackney-diamonds-review-1234837336/). So is there anything you might want to say about that?  
**_\[Watt smiles and holds up the Rolling Stones soccer jersey he’s wearing.\]_ I’ve said it before, it’s like working for Batman.  I’m Commissioner Gordon. Or it’s opposite, actually. When the bat sign goes up in the air, when the tongue is up in the air, you just go. When it’s time you go. I can say we did some recording together, but that’s all I can say.

**So what holds all this different work together in your mind as far as your approach?**  
The reason why I can work a lot and stay inspired is ’cause I get to work with all these different artists in all these different genres. If I was just making rock music, I feel like maybe the sound would get tired at a certain point, right? But if I got to make _Hackney Diamonds_ and then go make an album with Lady Gaga and be making dance music, I’m learning different things. I’m listening to different stuff. It’s a different part of my brain and requires a different skillset for me. But at the end of the day, it’s still listening to an artist and figuring out how to get what they want to say out into the world, into a record. Working across all different genres keeps everything exciting, and makes it refreshing when you get to go listen to a band play. And it makes it refreshing when you’re like, “Oh, we’re not recording a band now. I’m working with one person and I have one boss.” It’s all exciting.

**The last time we spoke, you said you were looking for a young rock band that could conquer the world. And the hunger for something like that seems to be out there — look at [those Oasis shows](https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-features/oasis-u-s-more-tour-dates-new-album-1235427875/).  
**I was there on Sunday!

## Trending Stories

**So is your head still there?**  
Absolutely. All the time. Any young band that anyone can show me, I’m the happiest person in the world. And what was so cool about Oasis is, like, they _are_ the zeitgeist. Just seeing L.A. come together like that, and young kids are there going crazy. Those songs, those guitar tones. The amps are up to 10. They just stand there and play and everyone goes crazy. How cool is that?

**Is there anything else upcoming that you can hint at?  
**I’m very busy!

# Pour Me A Drink by Post Malone (featuring Blake Shelton) - Songfacts

![Play Video](https://img.youtube.com/vi/RoeXmaSE7Lo/hqdefault.jpg)

#### Songfacts®:

*   "Pour Me a Drink" pairs Post Malone's signature drawl with Blake Shelton's down-home twang. Both fellas are ready to trade in their troubles for a barstool and a stiff drink come Friday night. Malone raps about everyday woes like a speeding ticket and a team's crushing defeat, while Shelton croons about a love gone south. But hey, misery loves company, right? They both could sure use a good pour.
    
*   The song itself is a fun, lighthearted toe-tapper penned by Malone and his go-to producer Louis Bell, along with some familiar names from the Morgan Wallen writing camp: Charlie Handsome, John Byron, Rocky Block, and Jordan Dozzi. Bell and Handsome cooked up a breezy country-pop instrumental that wouldn't sound out of place on Shelton's mid-'00s playlist.
    
*   First hinted at in late May 2024, "Pour Me a Drink" officially hit the airwaves on June 21, 2024, as the second single from Post Malone's country project **F-1 Trillion**.
    
*   Directed by Chris Villa (the same guy behind **F-1 Trillion**'s lead single "[I Had Some Help](https://www.songfacts.com/facts/post-malone/i-had-some-help)"), the video starts with Posty trying to score some brews at a gas station, with Blake Shelton manning the register. They head to a wild lakeside party, where the pair are surrounded by Bud Lights, a drink Malone always seems to have nearby.
    
*   During an _Entertainment Tonight_ interview, Blake Shelton credited Post Malone for reigniting his passion for making music after retiring from _The Voice_. Malone's enthusiasm and work ethic, which Shelton described as unparalleled, inspired him. The collaboration not only resulted in this song but also sparked a genuine friendship.
